        Collect all validation errors without short-circuiting
        Return sanitized params and error list

Behavior AuthenticateRequest
    Input:
        request: HttpRequest
        requiredRoles: list
    Output:
        authenticated: boolean
        userId: string
    Action:
        Extract session cookie from request headers
        Validate session ID and load session data
        Check user roles against required roles
        Verify IP and user-agent match session fingerprint
        Return authentication result

# Level 4: Conditions
Condition: SessionExpired
    When session lastAccessedAt exceeds configured TTL
    Then destroy session, clear cookie, and redirect to login with flash message

Condition: UnauthorizedAccess
    When authenticated user lacks required role for route
    Then return HTTP 403 with insufficient-privileges view and log attempt

Condition: ValidationFailure
    When input validation produces any errors
    Then re-render form view with error messages and preserved input values

# Level 5: Events
Event: OnRequestReceived
    On new HTTP request entering the middleware pipeline
    Action: Start request timer, inject correlation ID, and attach trace context

Event: OnAuthenticationFailure
    On session validation or role check failure
    Action: Log security event with IP and user-agent, increment failed auth metric

Event: OnSessionCreated
    On new session established after successful login
    Action: Emit audit event, set session cookie with Secure and HttpOnly flags

Event: OnRouteNotFound
    On no matching route found for request path and method
    Action: Return HTTP 404 with custom not-found view and log path for analysis

# Level 6: Concurrency
Parallel:
    Request handling across multiple worker processes
    Session store read/write operations with optimistic locking
    Template compilation for modified views in background
    Middleware execution for independent concerns (logging, metrics, CORS)
    Static asset serving on separate thread pool from dynamic requests

# Level 7: Optimization
Optimize: Request processing latency
    Priority: Cache compiled templates; pool database connections; minimize middleware overhead per route

Optimize: View rendering throughput
    Priority: Pre-compile templates at startup; cache rendered fragments with key-based expiration

# Level 8: Learning
Learn: Route popularity patterns
    Goal: Identify high-traffic routes for pre-warming and connection pool sizing
    Adapt: Per-route connection pool allocation
    Based: Request frequency distribution and latency percentiles over sliding 15-minute window

Learn: Session store sizing
    Goal: Predict session store memory requirements based on traffic patterns
    Adapt: Session TTL and eviction aggressiveness
    Based: Concurrent session count trends and average session data size

# Level 9: Security
Security:
    Encrypt: Session cookie using HMAC-SHA256 with rotating secret key
    Encrypt: Sensitive session data fields with AES-256-GCM server-side encryption
    Protect: All forms against CSRF with per-request token validation and SameSite cookies
    Protect: Application against XSS with Content-Security-Policy headers and auto-escaping
    Protect: Upload endpoints against file inclusion with mime-type validation and sandboxed storage

# Level 10: Native

{
package mvc

import (
    "crypto/hmac"
    "crypto/sha256"
    "encoding/hex"
    "fmt"
    "net/http"
    "regexp"
    "sync"
    "time"
)

type Route struct {
    Method      string
    Pattern     *regexp.Regexp
    Handler     http.HandlerFunc
    Middleware  []func(http.Handler) http.Handler
    Params      []string
}

type Router struct {
    routes []Route
    mu     sync.RWMutex
}

func NewRouter() *Router {
    return &Router{}
}

func (r *Router) AddRoute(method, pattern string, handler http.HandlerFunc, middleware ...func(http.Handler) http.Handler) {
    re := regexp.MustCompile(pattern)
    paramRe := regexp.MustCompile(`:([a-zA-Z]+)`)
    matches := paramRe.FindAllStringSubmatch(pattern, -1)
    params := make([]string, 0)
    for _, m := range matches {
        params = append(params, m[1])
    }
    r.mu.Lock()
    r.routes = append(r.routes, Route{
        Method: method, Pattern: re, Handler: handler,
        Middleware: middleware, Params: params,
    })
    r.mu.Unlock()
}

func (r *Router) ServeHTTP(w http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request) {
    r.mu.RLock()
    defer r.mu.RUnlock()
    for _, route := range r.routes {
        if route.Method != req.Method {
            continue
        }
        matches := route.Pattern.FindStringSubmatch(req.URL.Path)
        if matches == nil {
            continue
        }
        for i, name := range route.Params {
            if i+1 < len(matches) {
                req.URL.RawQuery += fmt.Sprintf("&%s=%s", name, matches[i+1])
            }
        }
        var handler http.Handler = route.Handler
        for i := len(route.Middleware) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
            handler = route.Middleware[i](handler)
        }
        handler.ServeHTTP(w, req)
        return
    }
    http.NotFound(w, req)
}

type SessionManager struct {
    store   map[string]*Session
    secret  []byte
    mu      sync.RWMutex
}

type Session struct {
    ID        string
    Data      map[string]interface{}
    CreatedAt time.Time
    ExpiresAt time.Time
    CSRFToken string
}

func NewSessionManager(secret string) *SessionManager {
    sm := &SessionManager{
        store:  make(map[string]*Session),
        secret: []byte(secret),
    }
    go sm.sweepExpired()
    return sm
}

func (sm *SessionManager) Create(w http.ResponseWriter) *Session {
    id := generateToken(sm.secret)
    session := &Session{
        ID: id, Data: make(map[string]interface{}),
        CreatedAt: time.Now(), ExpiresAt: time.Now().Add(30 * time.Minute),
        CSRFToken: generateToken(sm.secret),
    }
    sm.mu.Lock()
    sm.store[id] = session
    sm.mu.Unlock()
    http.SetCookie(w, &http.Cookie{
        Name: "session_id", Value: id,
        HttpOnly: true, Secure: true, SameSite: http.SameSiteStrictMode,
        Path: "/", MaxAge: 1800,
    })
    return session
}

func (sm *SessionManager) sweepExpired() {
    ticker := time.NewTicker(60 * time.Second)
    for range ticker.C {
        sm.mu.Lock()
        now := time.Now()
        for id, s := range sm.store {
            if now.After(s.ExpiresAt) {
                delete(sm.store, id)
            }
        }
        sm.mu.Unlock()
    }
}

func generateToken(secret []byte) string {
    h := hmac.New(sha256.New, secret)
    h.Write([]byte(fmt.Sprintf("%d", time.Now().UnixNano())))
    return hex.EncodeToString(h.Sum(nil))
}
}

description: AICL Example: Observer Pattern Event Bus Implements a robust publish/subscribe event bus with topic routing, guaranteed message ordering, backpressure management, dead letter queue handling, and replay capabilities.
instruction: Create an AICL specification for a observer pattern event bus. Include all 10 language levels: architecture (goals, constraints, risks with recovery, layers), entities, behaviors, conditions, events, concurrency, optimization, learning, security, and native code.
completion:
# AICL Example: Observer Pattern Event Bus
# Implements a robust publish/subscribe event bus with topic routing, guaranteed message ordering,
# backpressure management, dead letter queue handling, and replay capabilities.

# Level 1: Architecture
Goal: Build a high-throughput event bus implementing the Observer pattern with topic-based routing,
    strict per-topic message ordering, backpressure to protect slow subscribers,
    dead letter queues for poison messages, and replay support for missed events.

Constraint: Publishers must be decoupled from subscribers; no direct references allowed.
Constraint: Each topic maintains FIFO ordering within a partition key.
Constraint: Subscribers must acknowledge messages within a configurable timeout.
Constraint: Backpressure must be applied before memory pressure reaches critical threshold.
Constraint: Dead letter messages must never be silently dropped; always persisted for inspection.

Risk: Slow subscriber causes unbounded buffer growth
Recovery: Apply per-subscriber backpressure with configurable max buffer; overflow goes to DLQ

Risk: Message ordering violation under concurrent publishing
Recovery: Partition by routing key; single-writer per partition with sequencer

Risk: Dead letter queue grows unbounded without reprocessing
Recovery: Scheduled DLQ reprocessor with exponential backoff; alert at queue depth threshold

Risk: Subscriber crash loses in-flight messages
Recovery: Redeliver unacknowledged messages after visibility timeout with at-least-once guarantee

Risk: Topic routing misconfiguration routes messages to wrong subscribers
Recovery: Validate topic subscription patterns at registration; audit log all routing decisions

Risk: Replay floods subscribers with historical volume
Recovery: Throttle replay delivery rate; subscribers opt-in to replay with max throughput setting

Layer: Core
    SubLayer: Publisher
    SubLayer: TopicRouter
    SubLayer: PartitionManager
Layer: Subscription
    SubLayer: SubscriberRegistry
    SubLayer: SubscriptionManager
    SubLayer: AcknowledgmentTracker
Layer: Reliability
    SubLayer: BackpressureController

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Message {
    pub message_id: String,
    pub topic: String,
    pub partition_key: String,
    pub sequence_number: u64,
    pub payload: Vec<u8>,
    pub headers: HashMap<String, String>,
    pub published_at: Instant,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Subscription {
    pub subscription_id: String,
    pub subscriber_name: String,
    pub topic_pattern: String,
    pub max_in_flight: usize,
    pub ack_timeout: Duration,
    pub retry_max: u32,
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum DeliverStatus {
    Acknowledged,
    Failed(String),
    Timeout,
}

pub struct DeadLetterEntry {
    pub entry_id: String,
    pub original_message: Message,
    pub subscriber_name: String,
    pub failure_reason: String,
    pub failure_count: u32,
    pub first_failed_at: Instant,
    pub dead_lettered_at: Instant,
}

pub struct EventBus {
    topics: Arc<Mutex<HashMap<String, Vec<Message>>>>,
    subscriptions: Arc<Mutex<Vec<Subscription>>>,
    in_flight: Arc<Mutex<HashMap<String, (Message, Instant, u32)>>>,
    dead_letter_queue: Arc<Mutex<Vec<DeadLetterEntry>>>,
    max_buffer: usize,
}

impl EventBus {
    pub fn new(max_buffer: usize) -> Self {
        EventBus {
            topics: Arc::new(Mutex::new(HashMap::new())),
            subscriptions: Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new())),
            in_flight: Arc::new(Mutex::new(HashMap::new())),
            dead_letter_queue: Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new())),
            max_buffer,
        }
    }

    pub fn publish(&self, topic: &str, msg: Message) -> u64 {
        let mut topics = self.topics.lock().unwrap();
        let partition = topics.entry(topic.to_string()).or_insert_with(Vec::new);
        let seq = partition.len() as u64;
        let mut msg = msg;
        msg.sequence_number = seq;
        partition.push(msg.clone());
        seq
    }

    pub fn subscribe(&self, sub: Subscription) {
        let mut subs = self.subscriptions.lock().unwrap();
        subs.push(sub);
    }

    pub fn acknowledge(&self, subscription_id: &str, message_id: &str) -> bool {
        let mut in_flight = self.in_flight.lock().unwrap();
        in_flight.remove(&format!("{}:{}", subscription_id, message_id)).is_some()
    }

    pub fn check_timeouts(&self) {
        let mut in_flight = self.in_flight.lock().unwrap();
        let mut dlq = self.dead_letter_queue.lock().unwrap();
        let now = Instant::now();
        let expired: Vec<String> = in_flight.iter()
            .filter(|(_, (msg, sent_at, retries))| {
                now.duration_since(*sent_at) > Duration::from_secs(30) && *retries >= 3
            })
            .map(|(k, _)| k.clone())
            .collect();
        for key in expired {
            if let Some((msg, _, retries)) = in_flight.remove(&key) {
                dlq.push(DeadLetterEntry {
                    entry_id: format!("dlq-{}", msg.message_id),
                    original_message: msg,
                    subscriber_name: String::new(),
                    failure_reason: "ack_timeout_exceeded".to_string(),
                    failure_count: retries,
                    first_failed_at: now,
                    dead_lettered_at: now,
                });
            }
        }
    }

    pub fn dead_letter_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.dead_letter_queue.lock().unwrap().len()
    }
}

fn main() {
    let bus = EventBus::new(10_000);
    let sub = Subscription {
        subscription_id: "sub-1".to_string(),
        subscriber_name: "order-service".to_string(),
        topic_pattern: "orders.*".to_string(),
        max_in_flight: 50,
        ack_timeout: Duration::from_secs(30),
        retry_max: 3,
    };
    bus.subscribe(sub);
    let msg = Message {
        message_id: "msg-1".to_string(),
        topic: "orders.created".to_string(),
        partition_key: "order-123".to_string(),
        sequence_number: 0,
        payload: vec![],
        headers: HashMap::new(),
        published_at: Instant::now(),
    };
    let seq = bus.publish("orders.created", msg);
    println!("Published message with sequence: {}", seq);
}

# Implements a strategy pattern engine with dynamic algorithm selection, runtime strategy switching,

# Level 1: Architecture
Goal: Build a strategy pattern engine that enables runtime algorithm selection and switching,
    supports automated benchmarking for strategy comparison, allows strategy composition
    for complex operations, and provides graceful fallback when strategies fail.

Constraint: Each strategy must implement a common interface with identical input and output contracts.
Constraint: Strategy selection must be deterministic given the same context and input.
Constraint: Benchmarking must not affect production strategy execution latency.
Constraint: Strategy switching must be atomic with no in-flight operations using the old strategy.
Constraint: Composite strategies must maintain the execution order declared in composition.

Risk: Strategy switch during active execution causes inconsistent results
Recovery: Complete in-flight operations with old strategy; apply new strategy to subsequent requests only

Risk: Benchmark sample too small produces unreliable comparison

Risk: Composite strategy partial failure leaves partial output

Risk: Memory leak from accumulated benchmark data
Recovery: Sliding window of 1 hour for benchmark samples; compress older data into summary statistics

Risk: Strategy selection oscillates between equivalent strategies causing instability
Recovery: Hysteresis threshold requiring 10% improvement over incumbent before switching

Risk: Custom strategy injection compromises system integrity

import java.util.*;
import java.util.concurrent.*;
import java.util.function.Function;

public interface Strategy<I, O> {
    String getId();
    String getName();
    O execute(I input) throws StrategyException;
    boolean canHandle(I input);
    int getPriority();
}

public class StrategyException extends Exception {
    public StrategyException(String msg, Throwable cause) { super(msg, cause); }
}

public class StrategySelector<I, O> {
    private final Map<String, Strategy<I, O>> registry = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final Map<String, String> activeStrategies = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final Map<String, BenchmarkResult> benchmarks = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final double hysteresisThreshold = 0.10;

    public void register(Strategy<I, O> strategy) {
        registry.put(strategy.getId(), strategy);
    }

    public Strategy<I, O> select(String operationType, I input) {
        List<Strategy<I, O>> candidates = registry.values().stream()
            .filter(Strategy::canHandle)
            .filter(s -> s.canHandle(input))
            .sorted(Comparator.comparingInt(Strategy::getPriority).reversed())
            .toList();

        if (candidates.isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("No strategy available for: " + operationType);
        }

        String currentId = activeStrategies.get(operationType);
        Strategy<I, O> best = candidates.get(0);

        if (currentId != null && !currentId.equals(best.getId())) {
            Strategy<I, O> current = registry.get(currentId);
            BenchmarkResult currentBench = benchmarks.get(currentId);
            BenchmarkResult bestBench = benchmarks.get(best.getId());
            if (currentBench != null && bestBench != null) {
                double improvement = (currentBench.meanLatency - bestBench.meanLatency)
                    / currentBench.meanLatency;
                if (improvement < hysteresisThreshold) {
                    best = current;
                }
            }
        }
        activeStrategies.put(operationType, best.getId());
        return best;
    }

    public O executeWithFallback(String operationType, I input, List<Strategy<I, O>> fallbacks) {
        Strategy<I, O> primary = select(operationType, input);
        try {
            return primary.execute(input);
        } catch (StrategyException e) {
            for (Strategy<I, O> fallback : fallbacks) {
                try {
                    return fallback.execute(input);
                } catch (StrategyException ignored) {}
            }
            throw new RuntimeException("All strategies failed", e);
        }
    }
}

public class BenchmarkRunner<I, O> {
    private final int defaultSampleSize = 1000;

    public BenchmarkResult run(Strategy<I, O> strategy, Function<Void, I> inputGenerator, int sampleSize) {
        List<Long> latencies = new ArrayList<>();
        int errors = 0;

        for (int i = 0; i < sampleSize; i++) {
            I input = inputGenerator.apply(null);
            long start = System.nanoTime();
            try {
                strategy.execute(input);
            } catch (StrategyException e) {
                errors++;
            }
            latencies.add(System.nanoTime() - start);
        }

        Collections.sort(latencies);
        long sum = latencies.stream().mapToLong(Long::longValue).sum();
        double mean = (double) sum / sampleSize;
        long p50 = latencies.get((int)(sampleSize * 0.50));
        long p99 = latencies.get((int)(sampleSize * 0.99));

        return new BenchmarkResult(
            strategy.getId(), sampleSize, mean, p50, p99,
            (double) errors / sampleSize
        );
    }
}

record BenchmarkResult(
    String strategyId, int sampleSize, double meanLatency,
    long p50Latency, long p99Latency, double errorRate
) {}
}

# AICL Example: Factory Pattern System
# Implements a comprehensive factory pattern system with abstract factory, builder pattern,
# prototype-based cloning, lazy initialization, and dependency injection container integration.

# Level 1: Architecture
Goal: Build a factory pattern system that provides abstract factories for product families,
    builder pattern for complex object construction, prototype registry for efficient cloning,
    lazy initialization for deferred resource allocation, and DI container integration for
    automatic dependency resolution and lifecycle management.

Constraint: Factories must return abstract types; concrete types never exposed to consumers.
Constraint: Builder steps must be validated in order before build() is called.
Constraint: Prototype clones must be deep copies with no shared mutable references.
Constraint: Lazy instances must be thread-safe on first access.
Constraint: DI container must detect circular dependencies at registration time.

Risk: Circular dependency causes infinite resolution loop
Recovery: Detect cycles via graph traversal at registration; throw descriptive error with dependency chain

Risk: Prototype shallow clone leaks shared state
Recovery: Enforce deep copy validation via serialization round-trip test at prototype registration

Risk: Builder incomplete construction produces invalid object
Recovery: Validate all required fields before build; throw with list of missing fields

Risk: Lazy initialization race condition creates duplicate instances
Recovery: Use double-checked locking with volatile reference; only one thread creates instance

Risk: Factory produces object with unresolved dependencies
Recovery: Validate dependency graph completeness before factory invocation; fail-fast with missing list

Risk: Memory leak from singleton accumulation in DI container
Recovery: Implement disposable lifecycle; container shutdown triggers dispose on all singletons

import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicReference
import java.util.concurrent.locks.ReentrantLock

interface Product {
    val id: String
    val type: String
    fun validate(): Boolean
}

data class ConcreteProductA(
    override val id: String,
    override val type: String = "A",
    val name: String,
    val value: Int,
    val metadata: Map<String, String> = emptyMap()
) : Product {
    override fun validate(): Boolean = id.isNotBlank() && name.isNotBlank()
}

data class ConcreteProductB(
    override val id: String,
    override val type: String = "B",
    val label: String,
    val score: Double,
    val tags: Set<String> = emptySet()
) : Product {
    override fun validate(): Boolean = id.isNotBlank() && label.isNotBlank()
}

interface AbstractFactory {
    fun create(parameters: Map<String, Any>): Product
}

class ProductAFactory : AbstractFactory {
    override fun create(parameters: Map<String, Any>): Product {
        return ConcreteProductA(
            id = parameters["id"] as String,
            name = parameters["name"] as String,
            value = parameters["value"] as Int,
            metadata = parameters["metadata"] as? Map<String, String> ?: emptyMap()
        )
    }
}

class ProductBFactory : AbstractFactory {
    override fun create(parameters: Map<String, Any>): Product {
        return ConcreteProductB(
            id = parameters["id"] as String,
            label = parameters["label"] as String,
            score = parameters["score"] as Double,
            tags = parameters["tags"] as? Set<String> ?: emptySet()
        )
    }
}

class ProductBuilder<T : Product>(private val factory: AbstractFactory) {
    private val steps = mutableMapOf<String, Any>()
    private val required = mutableListOf<String>()

    fun withStep(name: String, value: Any, isRequired: Boolean = false): ProductBuilder<T> {
        steps[name] = value
        if (isRequired) required.add(name)
        return this
    }

    fun build(): T {
        val missing = required.filter { it !in steps.keys }
        require(missing.isEmpty()) { "Missing required steps: $missing" }
        return factory.create(steps) as T
    }
}

class PrototypeRegistry {
    private val prototypes = ConcurrentHashMap<String, Product>()

    fun register(key: String, prototype: Product) {
        val clone = deepClone(prototype)
        require(clone !== prototype) { "Shallow clone detected for $key" }
        prototypes[key] = prototype
    }

    fun clone(key: String, overrides: Map<String, Any> = emptyMap()): Product {
        val original = prototypes[key] ?: throw IllegalArgumentException("No prototype: $key")
        val cloned = deepClone(original)
        return applyOverrides(cloned, overrides)
    }

    private fun deepClone(product: Product): Product = when (product) {
        is ConcreteProductA -> product.copy(metadata = product.metadata.toMap())
        is ConcreteProductB -> product.copy(tags = product.tags.toSet())
        else -> throw IllegalArgumentException("Unknown product type")
    }

    private fun applyOverrides(product: Product, overrides: Map<String, Any>): Product {
        return product
    }
}

class LazyInitializer<T>(private val factory: () -> T) {
    private val ref = AtomicReference<T?>()
    private val lock = ReentrantLock()

    val instance: T
        get() {
            ref.get()?.let { return it }
            lock.lock()
            try {
                ref.get()?.let { return it }
                val created = factory()
                ref.set(created)
                return created
            } finally {
                lock.unlock()
            }
        }
}

class DIContainer {
    private val registrations = mutableMapOf<Class<*>, DIReg<*>>()
    private val singletons = ConcurrentHashMap<Class<*>, Any>()

    data class DIReg<T>(
        val type: Class<T>,
        val factory: (DIContainer) -> T,
        val lifetime: Lifetime
    )

    enum class Lifetime { SINGLETON, SCOPPED, TRANSIENT }

    inline fun <reified T> register(noinline factory: (DIContainer) -> T, lifetime: Lifetime) {
        registrations[T::class.java] = DIReg(T::class.java, factory, lifetime)
    }

    @Suppress("UNCHECKED_CAST")
    fun <T> resolve(type: Class<T>): T {
        val reg = registrations[type] as? DIReg<T>
            ?: throw IllegalArgumentException("No registration for ${type.name}")
        return when (reg.lifetime) {
            Lifetime.SINGLETON -> singletons.getOrPut(type) { reg.factory(this) } as T
            Lifetime.TRANSIENT -> reg.factory(this)
            Lifetime.SCOPPED -> reg.factory(this)
        }
    }
}

fun main() {
    val registry = PrototypeRegistry()
    registry.register("productA", ConcreteProductA("proto-1", name = "Prototype", value = 42))
    val cloned = registry.clone("productA")
    println("Cloned: $cloned")

    val lazy = LazyInitializer { ConcreteProductB("lazy-1", label = "Lazy", score = 99.9) }
    println("Lazy instance: ${lazy.instance}")
}

# AICL Example: Plugin Architecture System
# Implements a dynamic plugin architecture with runtime loading, sandboxing, API versioning,
# dependency resolution between plugins, hot reload capabilities, and plugin lifecycle management.

# Level 1: Architecture
Goal: Build a plugin architecture system supporting dynamic loading and unloading of plugins at runtime,
    sandboxed execution to isolate plugin failures, versioned APIs for backward compatibility,
    automatic dependency resolution between plugins, and hot reload without service interruption.

Constraint: Plugins must not access host internals except through declared API surfaces.
Constraint: Each plugin must declare its API version requirement; mismatched versions are rejected.
Constraint: Plugin sandbox must limit CPU, memory, and I/O to configured quotas.
Constraint: Hot reload must not interrupt in-flight requests using the old plugin version.
Conseint: Plugin dependency cycles must be detected and rejected at installation time.

Risk: Malicious plugin escapes sandbox and accesses host resources
Recovery: Kill plugin process immediately; audit all accessed resources; blacklist plugin signature

Risk: Plugin hot reload leaves orphaned event listeners or timers
Recovery: Track all registered callbacks per plugin; revoke and clean up on unload before activating new version

Risk: API version mismatch causes runtime errors in dependent plugins
Recovery: Validate version compatibility graph before loading; isolate incompatible plugins to separate sandbox

Risk: Plugin memory leak degrades host performance
Recovery: Enforce per-plugin memory quota; automatically unload plugin exceeding limit with notification

Risk: Circular plugin dependency prevents any plugin from loading
Recovery: Detect cycles at installation; reject with clear dependency chain visualization

Risk: Plugin load failure crashes host application
Recovery: Isolate plugin initialization in try-catch with fallback; mark plugin as failed without affecting host

    SubLayer: PluginLoader
    SubLayer: PluginRegistry
    SubLayer: LifecycleManager
Layer: Isolation
    SubLayer: SandboxRuntime

Validation: Plugin manifest must declare name, version, API version, and dependencies

Validation: All plugin dependencies must be satisfied before activation

import importlib
import importlib.util
import sys
import threading
import traceback
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, List, Optional
from enum import Enum
import time

class PluginState(Enum):
    LOADED = "loaded"
    ACTIVATED = "activated"
    DEACTIVATING = "deactivating"
    DEACTIVATED = "deactivated"
    FAILED = "failed"

@dataclass
class PluginManifest:
    plugin_id: str
    plugin_name: str
    version: str
    api_version: str
    dependencies: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    permissions: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    entry_point: str = "main"
    description: str = ""
    author: str = ""

@dataclass
class SandboxConfig:
    sandbox_id: str
    max_memory_mb: int = 256
    max_cpu_percent: float = 50.0
    network_access: bool = False
    allowed_apis: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    timeout_seconds: int = 30

class PluginSandbox:
    def __init__(self, config: SandboxConfig):
        self.config = config
        self.memory_usage = 0
        self.violation_count = 0
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    def check_permission(self, api_name: str) -> bool:
        if api_name in self.config.allowed_apis:
            return True
        with self._lock:
            self.violation_count += 1
        return False

    def check_memory(self, used_mb: int) -> bool:
        if used_mb <= self.config.max_memory_mb:
            self.memory_usage = used_mb
            return True
        return False

class PluginInstance:
    def __init__(self, manifest: PluginManifest, sandbox: PluginSandbox):
        self.instance_id = f"{manifest.plugin_id}-{manifest.version}"
        self.manifest = manifest
        self.sandbox = sandbox
        self.state = PluginState.LOADED
        self.module = None
        self.request_count = 0
        self.error_count = 0
        self.loaded_at = time.time()

class PluginManager:
    def __init__(self):
        self.plugins: Dict[str, PluginInstance] = {}
        self.api_versions: Dict[str, Dict] = {}
        self._dependency_graph: Dict[str, List[str]] = {}
        self._lock = threading.RLock()

    def register_api_version(self, version: str, surface: Dict):
        self.api_versions[version] = surface

    def load_plugin(self, manifest: PluginManifest, sandbox_config: SandboxConfig) -> str:
        with self._lock:
            if not self._check_api_compatibility(manifest.api_version):
                raise ValueError(f"API version {manifest.api_version} incompatible")

            if not self._resolve_dependencies(manifest):
                raise ValueError(f"Unresolved dependencies for {manifest.plugin_id}")

            if self._detect_cycle(manifest.plugin_id, manifest.dependencies):
                raise ValueError(f"Circular dependency detected for {manifest.plugin_id}")

            sandbox = PluginSandbox(sandbox_config)
            instance = PluginInstance(manifest, sandbox)
            sandbox.check_permission("lifecycle.install")

            instance.state = PluginState.ACTIVATED
            self.plugins[manifest.plugin_id] = instance
            self._dependency_graph[manifest.plugin_id] = manifest.dependencies

            return instance.instance_id

    def unload_plugin(self, plugin_id: str, graceful: bool = True) -> str:
        with self._lock:
            instance = self.plugins.get(plugin_id)
            if not instance:
                return f"Plugin {plugin_id} not found"

            instance.state = PluginState.DEACTIVATING
            if graceful and instance.request_count > 0:
                timeout = 30
                start = time.time()
                while instance.request_count > 0 and (time.time() - start) < timeout:
                    time.sleep(0.1)

            instance.state = PluginState.DEACTIVATED
            del self.plugins[plugin_id]
            self._dependency_graph.pop(plugin_id, None)
            return f"Plugin {plugin_id} unloaded successfully"

    def hot_reload(self, plugin_id: str, new_manifest: PluginManifest) -> str:
        old_instance = self.plugins.get(plugin_id)
        if not old_instance:
            return f"Plugin {plugin_id} not found for hot reload"

        old_version = old_instance.manifest.version
        sandbox_config = old_instance.sandbox.config

        try:
            new_instance_id = self.load_plugin(new_manifest, sandbox_config)
            self.unload_plugin(plugin_id, graceful=True)
            return f"Hot reload: {old_version} -> {new_manifest.version} ({new_instance_id})"
        except Exception as e:
            return f"Hot reload failed: {str(e)}, old version still active"

    def _check_api_compatibility(self, api_version: str) -> bool:
        return api_version in self.api_versions

    def _resolve_dependencies(self, manifest: PluginManifest) -> bool:
        for dep in manifest.dependencies:
            if dep not in self.plugins:
                return False
        return True

    def _detect_cycle(self, plugin_id: str, dependencies: List[str]) -> bool:
        visited = set()
        def dfs(node: str) -> bool:
            if node in visited:
                return True
            visited.add(node)
            for dep in self._dependency_graph.get(node, []):
                if dfs(dep):
                    return True
            visited.discard(node)
            return False
        self._dependency_graph[plugin_id] = dependencies
        result = dfs(plugin_id)
        if result:
            self._dependency_graph.pop(plugin_id, None)
        return result

manager = PluginManager()
manager.register_api_version("1.0", {"execute": True, "query": True})
manifest = PluginManifest("auth-plugin", "Auth Plugin", "1.0.0", "1.0", [])
config = SandboxConfig("sandbox-1", allowed_apis=["lifecycle.install", "execute"])
instance_id = manager.load_plugin(manifest, config)
print(f"Loaded: {instance_id}")
}

# AICL Example: Hexagonal Architecture
# Implements a hexagonal (ports and adapters) architecture with clean domain core isolation,
# inbound and outbound ports, infrastructure adapters, and comprehensive testability guarantees.

# Level 1: Architecture
Goal: Build a hexagonal architecture that isolates the domain core from all infrastructure concerns,
    defines explicit ports for inbound (driving) and outbound (driven) interactions,
    provides swappable adapters for each port, and guarantees the domain is fully testable
    without any infrastructure dependency.

Constraint: Domain core must have zero imports from infrastructure or framework packages.
Constraint: All external interactions must flow through declared ports with defined interfaces.
Constraint: Adapters must depend on ports; ports must never depend on adapters.
Constraint: Each port must have at least one production adapter and one test adapter.
Constraint: Domain events must be defined in the domain and published through an outbound port.

Risk: Domain logic leaks into adapter implementation
Recovery: Enforce dependency rule via architectural fitness functions in CI; auto-fail builds on violation

Risk: Port interface too generic reduces domain expressiveness
Recovery: Design ports with domain-specific method names; avoid generic CRUD-style port interfaces

Risk: Adapter state inconsistency during domain operation
Recovery: Wrap multi-port operations in unit of work; ensure atomic commit across adapters

Risk: Test adapter diverges from production adapter behavior
Recovery: Run contract tests against both adapters; validate output equivalence for same inputs

Risk: Infrastructure exception propagates into domain core
Recovery: Adapter must catch and translate all infrastructure exceptions to domain error types at port boundary

Risk: Missing adapter for required port at startup
Recovery: Validate all ports have registered adapters at application bootstrap; fail fast with missing list

    Encrypt: Domain event payloads containing PII before passing to outbound port adapters

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Type
from enum import Enum
import time
from contextlib import contextmanager

# ===================== DOMAIN CORE =====================

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class OrderId:
    value: str

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Money:
    amount: float
    currency: str

class OrderStatus(Enum):
    DRAFT = "draft"
    CONFIRMED = "confirmed"
    SHIPPED = "shipped"
    CANCELLED = "cancelled"

@dataclass
class LineItem:
    product_id: str
    quantity: int
    unit_price: Money

class Order:
    def __init__(self, order_id: OrderId, customer_id: str):
        self._order_id = order_id
        self._customer_id = customer_id
        self._items: List[LineItem] = []
        self._status = OrderStatus.DRAFT
        self._events: List['DomainEvent'] = []

    @property
    def order_id(self) -> OrderId:
        return self._order_id

    @property
    def status(self) -> OrderStatus:
        return self._status

    @property
    def total(self) -> Money:
        if not self._items:
            return Money(0.0, "USD")
        total = sum(i.quantity * i.unit_price.amount for i in self._items)
        return Money(total, self._items[0].unit_price.currency)

    def add_item(self, item: LineItem) -> None:
        self._validate_status(OrderStatus.DRAFT)
        self._items.append(item)

    def confirm(self) -> None:
        self._validate_status(OrderStatus.DRAFT)
        if not self._items:
            raise ValueError("Cannot confirm empty order")
        self._status = OrderStatus.CONFIRMED
        self._events.append(OrderConfirmedEvent(
            aggregate_id=self._order_id.value,
            total=self.total.amount
        ))

    def cancel(self) -> None:
        if self._status == OrderStatus.SHIPPED:
            raise ValueError("Cannot cancel shipped order")
        self._status = OrderStatus.CANCELLED

    def _validate_status(self, expected: OrderStatus) -> None:
        if self._status != expected:
            raise ValueError(f"Expected {expected.value}, got {self._status.value}")

    def pop_events(self) -> List['DomainEvent']:
        events = self._events[:]
        self._events.clear()
        return events

@dataclass
class DomainEvent:
    event_type: str
    aggregate_id: str
    payload: Dict[str, Any]
    occurred_at: float = field(default_factory=time.time)

@dataclass
class OrderConfirmedEvent(DomainEvent):
    aggregate_id: str
    total: float
    event_type: str = "order.confirmed"
    payload: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

# ===================== PORTS =====================

class OrderRepositoryPort(ABC):
    @abstractmethod
    def find_by_id(self, order_id: OrderId) -> Optional[Order]:
        pass

    @abstractmethod
    def save(self, order: Order) -> None:
        pass

class EventPublisherPort(ABC):
    @abstractmethod
    def publish(self, events: List[DomainEvent]) -> None:
        pass

class NotificationPort(ABC):
    @abstractmethod
    def send_order_confirmation(self, customer_id: str, order_id: str, total: float) -> None:
        pass

# ===================== USE CASES =====================

class ConfirmOrderUseCase:
    def __init__(self, repo: OrderRepositoryPort, publisher: EventPublisherPort,
                 notifier: NotificationPort):
        self._repo = repo
        self._publisher = publisher
        self._notifier = notifier

    def execute(self, order_id: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        oid = OrderId(order_id)
        order = self._repo.find_by_id(oid)
        if not order:
            raise ValueError(f"Order {order_id} not found")

        order.confirm()
        self._repo.save(order)

        events = order.pop_events()
        self._publisher.publish(events)

        for event in events:
            if isinstance(event, OrderConfirmedEvent):
                self._notifier.send_order_confirmation(
                    order._customer_id, order_id, event.total
                )

        return {"order_id": order_id, "status": order.status.value}

# ===================== ADAPTERS =====================

class InMemoryOrderRepository(OrderRepositoryPort):
    def __init__(self):
        self._store: Dict[str, Order] = {}

    def find_by_id(self, order_id: OrderId) -> Optional[Order]:
        return self._store.get(order_id.value)

    def save(self, order: Order) -> None:
        self._store[order.order_id.value] = order

class ConsoleEventPublisher(EventPublisherPort):
    def publish(self, events: List[DomainEvent]) -> None:
        for event in events:
            print(f"[EVENT] {event.event_type}: {event.aggregate_id}")

class ConsoleNotification(NotificationPort):
    def send_order_confirmation(self, customer_id: str, order_id: str, total: float) -> None:
        print(f"[NOTIFY] Customer {customer_id}: Order {order_id} confirmed, total: ${total:.2f}")

# ===================== WIRED APPLICATION =====================

repo = InMemoryOrderRepository()
publisher = ConsoleEventPublisher()
notifier = ConsoleNotification()
use_case = ConfirmOrderUseCase(repo, publisher, notifier)

order = Order(OrderId("ORD-001"), "CUST-42")
order.add_item(LineItem("PROD-A", 2, Money(29.99, "USD")))
order.add_item(LineItem("PROD-B", 1, Money(49.99, "USD")))
repo.save(order)

result = use_case.execute("ORD-001")
print(f"Result: {result}")
}

description: AICL Example: Distributed Consensus System Implements a Raft-based distributed consensus protocol with leader election, log replication, split-brain prevention, and commit index management for strongly consistent state machines.
instruction: Create an AICL specification for a distributed consensus system. Include all 10 language levels: architecture (goals, constraints, risks with recovery, layers), entities, behaviors, conditions, events, concurrency, optimization, learning, security, and native code.
completion:
# AICL Example: Distributed Consensus System
# Implements a Raft-based distributed consensus protocol with leader election, log replication,
# split-brain prevention, and commit index management for strongly consistent state machines.

# Level 1: Architecture
Goal: Provide a fault-tolerant distributed consensus mechanism ensuring linearizable consistency across a cluster of nodes using the Raft protocol, with automatic leader election, log replication, and split-brain prevention.

Constraint: Quorum must be maintained with (N/2 + 1) nodes for any state mutation
Constraint: Leader election timeout must be randomized between 150ms-300ms to prevent split votes
Constraint: Log entries must be committed only after replication to a majority of nodes
Constraint: Term numbers must be monotonically increasing and never reused
Constraint: Candidates must increment term before requesting votes

Risk: Network partition causing split-brain with dual leaders
Recovery: Enforce strict term-based leadership; nodes in minority partition automatically step down to follower when detecting higher term from majority partition heartbeat

Risk: Leader failure during log replication leaving followers with divergent logs
Recovery: Followers truncate conflicting log entries beyond the last agreed-upon index and re-replicate from the new leader's log using AppendEntries consistency check

Risk: Split vote during leader election with no candidate achieving majority
Recovery: Randomized election timeouts ensure candidates retry at staggered intervals; subsequent election round produces a clear winner with high probability

Risk: Stale leader continuing to serve requests after network partition heals
Recovery: Stale leader detects higher term in AppendEntries or RequestVote response and immediately steps down to follower, discarding uncommitted entries

Risk: Log divergence across nodes due to missed entries during transient failures
Recovery: Leader maintains nextIndex and matchIndex per follower; decrements nextIndex on consistency failure and re-sends entries from the point of divergence

Risk: Quorum loss causing complete system unavailability
Recovery: Remaining nodes enter pre-vote candidate state; system remains in degraded read-only mode until quorum is restored; write operations are rejected with explicit error

Layer: ConsensusCore
    SubLayer: LeaderElection
    SubLayer: LogReplication
    SubLayer: CommitManagement
    SubLayer: SafetyGuarantees
Layer: ClusterManagement
    SubLayer: MembershipTracking
    SubLayer: ConfigurationChange
    SubLayer: SnapshotRecovery
Layer: ClientInterface
    SubLayer: RequestRouting
    SubLayer: ResponseCoalescing

Validation: Quorum must be achievable before accepting any write operation
Validation: Leader term must be strictly greater than all previous terms observed by a majority
Validation: Committed entries must never be overwritten or truncated across any node
Validation: Leader completeness property — any committed entry must be present in the log of any future leader
Validation: Log matching property — if two entries at the same index share the same term, all preceding entries must be identical
Validation: Election safety — at most one leader can exist per term
Validation: Snapshot last_included_index must never exceed the commit index

# Level 2: Entities
Entity ConsensusNode
    nodeId: string
    currentTerm: integer
    votedFor: string
    log: list
    commitIndex: integer
    lastApplied: integer
    state: string
    leaderId: string
    electionTimeout: float
    heartbeatInterval: float

Entity LogEntry
    index: integer
    term: integer
    command: bytes
    clientRequestId: string
    timestamp: datetime
    isCommitted: boolean
    snapshotBoundary: boolean

Entity LeaderState
    nextIndex: dict
    matchIndex: dict
    replicationInProgress: dict
    lastHeartbeatSent: datetime
    pendingClientRequests: list
    leaseExpiry: datetime

Entity ClusterConfig
    nodes: list
    votingMembers: set
    nonVotingMembers: set
    jointConfiguration: boolean
    configurationIndex: integer
    version: integer
    minElectionTimeout: float
    maxElectionTimeout: float

Entity Snapshot
    lastIncludedIndex: integer
    lastIncludedTerm: integer
    stateMachineData: bytes
    configuration: dict
    createdAt: datetime
    sizeBytes: integer
    checksum: string

Entity VoteRequest
    candidateId: string
    term: integer
    lastLogIndex: integer
    lastLogTerm: integer
    priority: integer
    preVote: boolean

Entity AppendEntriesRequest
    leaderId: string
    term: integer
    prevLogIndex: integer
    prevLogTerm: integer
    entries: list
    leaderCommit: integer
    leaseDuration: float

# Level 3: Behaviors
Behavior RequestVote
    Input: voteRequest: VoteRequest
    Output: term: integer, voteGranted: boolean
    Action:
        If voteRequest.term < currentTerm, reject with currentTerm
        If voteRequest.preVote is true, evaluate log-up-to-date without updating term
        If votedFor is null or equals candidateId, and candidate log is at least as up-to-date, grant vote
        Reset election timer upon granting vote
        Persist votedFor to stable storage before responding

Behavior AppendEntries
    Input: appendRequest: AppendEntriesRequest
    Output: term: integer, success: boolean, conflictIndex: integer, conflictTerm: integer
    Action:
        If appendRequest.term < currentTerm, reject immediately
        If prevLogIndex exceeds log length, return conflictIndex = len(log) and conflictTerm = None
        If log[prevLogIndex].term != prevLogTerm, find conflictTerm and earliest conflictIndex
        Truncate any conflicting entries beyond matching prefix
        Append new entries not already in log
        If leaderCommit > commitIndex, advance commitIndex to min(leaderCommit, index of last new entry)
        Reset election timer to prevent unnecessary election

Behavior BecomeLeader
    Input: term: integer, nodeId: string
    Output: void
    Action:
        Transition state to leader
        Initialize nextIndex for all peers to lastLogIndex + 1
        Initialize matchIndex for all peers to 0
        Append no-op entry to log to commit entries from previous terms
        Begin sending periodic heartbeats with lease duration
        Acquire leader lease for read requests

Behavior SubmitCommand
    Input: command: bytes, clientRequestId: string
    Output: index: integer, term: integer, isCommitted: boolean
    Action:
        Validate leader state; redirect to current leader if follower
        Append entry to local log with current term
        Replicate entry to all followers via AppendEntries
        Wait for majority acknowledgment
        Advance commit index
        Apply to state machine once committed
        Respond to client with commit confirmation

Behavior InstallSnapshot
    Input: leaderId: string, term: integer, lastIncludedIndex: integer, lastIncludedTerm: integer, data: bytes, offset: integer, done: boolean
    Output: term: integer
    Action:
        Validate term; reject if stale
        If snapshot lastIncludedIndex <= lastApplied, discard and acknowledge
        If partial snapshot, write data at offset to temporary snapshot buffer
        If done is true, discard log entries covered by snapshot
        Reset state machine with snapshot data
        Persist snapshot to stable storage
        Update lastIncludedIndex and lastIncludedTerm

Behavior TransferLeadership
    Input: targetId: string, timeout: float
    Output: success: boolean, newLeaderId: string
    Action:
        Stop accepting new client requests
        If target is not up-to-date, send AppendEntries to bring it current
        Send TimeoutNow request to target node
        Target node starts immediate election with minimal timeout
        Wait for new leader to emerge within timeout
        Resume accepting requests under new leader

Behavior AdvanceCommitIndex
    Input: void
    Output: newCommitIndex: integer
    Action:
        Find highest index N such that N > commitIndex and majority of matchIndex[i] >= N
        Verify log[N].term == currentTerm (only commit entries from current term)
        Set commitIndex = N
        Apply all entries between lastApplied and commitIndex to state machine
        Return new commit index

# Level 4: Conditions
Condition: LeaderStepDown
    When leader receives RequestVote or AppendEntries with term > currentTerm
    Then immediately transition to follower state, update currentTerm, reset votedFor, and abort pending client requests

Condition: ElectionTimeoutExpired
    When election timer fires without receiving valid heartbeat from leader
    Then increment currentTerm, transition to candidate state, vote for self, and broadcast RequestVote to all peers

Condition: QuorumLost
    When number of responsive nodes falls below (totalNodes / 2 + 1)
    Then leader steps down to follower, all write operations are rejected, system enters read-only degraded mode, and alert is emitted to cluster operator

Condition: LogConflictDetected
    When AppendEntries consistency check fails at prevLogIndex
    Then decrement nextIndex for that follower and retry AppendEntries with earlier log entries until consistency point is found

Condition: ConfigChangeUnsafe
    When joint consensus configuration change is in progress and a second change is attempted
    Then reject the second configuration change until the first is committed; only one config change may be outstanding at a time

# Level 5: Events
Event: OnLeaderElected
    On new leader confirmed by majority votes
    Action: Initialize leader state, emit leadership transition metric, notify client redirect service, begin heartbeat cycle, append no-op entry to commit prior term entries

Event: OnLogCommitted
    On entry committed at new commit index
    Action: Apply entry to state machine, respond to waiting client, emit latency metric from submission to commit, update lastApplied index, trigger snapshot if log size exceeds threshold

Event: OnNodeJoined
    On new node added to cluster configuration
    Action: Add to non-voting members initially, begin log catchup via AppendEntries, promote to voting member once caught up, update cluster configuration with joint consensus, broadcast new config

Event: OnSnapshotCreated
    On snapshot completed and persisted
    Action: Truncate log entries covered by snapshot, emit snapshot size metric, update lastIncludedIndex, notify peers of new snapshot availability, free memory from compacted log entries

Event: OnFollowerLagDetected
    On follower matchIndex falls behind commitIndex by more than 1000 entries
    Action: Switch to sending InstallSnapshot instead of incremental AppendEntries, emit lag warning metric, consider throttling client submissions if replication backlog grows unbounded

# Level 6: Concurrency
Parallel:
    Leader heartbeat broadcast to all followers
    Log replication streams to individual followers
    State machine application of committed entries
    Snapshot creation on background thread
    Client request acknowledgment processing

# Level 7: Optimization
Optimize: Log replication throughput
    Priority: Batch multiple log entries into a single AppendEntries RPC when follower is behind, reducing round trips; pipeline AppendEntries requests to overlapping followers to maximize network utilization

Optimize: Leader election latency
    Priority: Use pre-vote protocol to avoid disruptive elections from partitioned nodes; prioritize nodes with more complete logs as election candidates to reduce post-election catchup

Optimize: Read request serving
    Priority: Implement leader lease-based reads without logging; serve read-only requests from followers using ReadIndex protocol for linearizable reads without write latency impact

# Level 8: Learning
Learn: Optimal election timeout for current network conditions
    Goal: Minimize leader election latency while avoiding unnecessary elections from transient network delays
    Adapt: electionTimeout range
    Based: Observed round-trip times to peers and historical false election rates over sliding 1000-election window

Learn: Optimal batch size for AppendEntries
    Goal: Maximize replication throughput without causing excessive memory pressure or latency spikes
    Adapt: maxEntriesPerBatch
    Based: Follower response times and network bandwidth utilization metrics over the last 60 seconds

Learn: Snapshot trigger threshold
    Goal: Balance log compaction frequency against snapshot I/O overhead
    Adapt: snapshotThreshold (log size in bytes before triggering snapshot)
    Based: Snapshot creation duration, disk I/O load, and application read/write ratio over the last 100 snapshots

# Level 9: Security
Security:
    Encrypt: All RPC communication between nodes using TLS 1.3 with mutual certificate authentication
    Encrypt: Snapshot data at rest using AES-256-GCM
    Encrypt: Vote persistence records on stable storage
    Protect: Leader election against unauthorized nodes by validating cluster membership certificates
    Protect: Log entries against tampering by computing Merkle hash chains across term boundaries
    Protect: Client request integrity by requiring signed clientRequestId with replay protection nonce
    Protect: Configuration change requests against unauthorized modification via multi-party authorization

# Level 10: Native
Native: Go

package raft

import (
    "context"
    "sync"
    "time"
)

type State int

const (
    Follower State = iota
    Candidate
    Leader
)

type Node struct {
    mu              sync.RWMutex
    id              string
    state           State
    currentTerm     uint64
    votedFor        string
    log             []*LogEntry
    commitIndex     uint64
    lastApplied     uint64
    nextIndex       map[string]uint64
    matchIndex      map[string]uint64
    heartbeatTick   *time.Ticker
    electionTimer   *time.Timer
    config          *ClusterConfig
    stateMachine    StateMachine
    snapshotStore   SnapshotStore
    transport       Transport
    applyCh         chan *LogEntry
    stopCh          chan struct{}
}

func (n *Node) Run(ctx context.Context) {
    for {
        select {
        case <-n.electionTimer.C:
            n.startElection()
        case <-n.heartbeatTick.C:
            if n.state == Leader {
                n.broadcastHeartbeat()
            }
        case entry := <-n.applyCh:
            n.stateMachine.Apply(entry.Command)
        case <-ctx.Done():
            n.shutdown()
            return
        }
    }
}

func (n *Node) startElection() {
    n.mu.Lock()
    n.state = Candidate
    n.currentTerm++
    n.votedFor = n.id
    term := n.currentTerm
    lastIdx, lastTerm := n.lastLogInfo()
    n.mu.Unlock()

    votesReceived := 1
    quorum := len(n.config.VotingMembers)/2 + 1

    for _, peer := range n.config.VotingMembers {
        if peer == n.id {
            continue
        }
        go func(peerID string) {
            resp, err := n.transport.RequestVote(peerID, &VoteRequest{
                CandidateId:  n.id,
                Term:         term,
                LastLogIndex: lastIdx,
                LastLogTerm:  lastTerm,
            })
            if err != nil {
                return
            }
            n.mu.Lock()
            defer n.mu.Unlock()
            if resp.Term > n.currentTerm {
                n.becomeFollower(resp.Term)
                return
            }
            if resp.VoteGranted && n.state == Candidate {
                votesReceived++
                if votesReceived >= quorum {
                    n.becomeLeader()
                }
            }
        }(peer)
    }
    n.resetElectionTimer()
}

func (n *Node) becomeLeader() {
    n.state = Leader
    lastIdx := n.lastLogIndex()
    for peer := range n.nextIndex {
        n.nextIndex[peer] = lastIdx + 1
        n.matchIndex[peer] = 0
    }
    n.appendNoOp()
}

# AICL Example: Service Mesh
# Implements a service mesh with sidecar proxy pattern, mutual TLS, traffic management,
# distributed tracing, observability, and policy enforcement across microservices.

# Level 1: Architecture
Goal: Provide a transparent infrastructure layer for service-to-service communication that enforces security, reliability, and observability policies without requiring application code changes, using a sidecar proxy model with centralized control plane.

Constraint: All inter-service traffic must traverse the sidecar proxy; direct pod-to-pod communication is prohibited
Constraint: mTLS must be established before any application payload is exchanged between services
Constraint: Control plane must remain operational even if individual sidecar proxies fail
Constraint: Policy changes must propagate to all sidecars within 10 seconds
Constraint: Sidecar proxy overhead must not exceed 5ms P99 latency addition per hop

Risk: Sidecar proxy failure causing complete communication blackout for a service instance
Recovery: Automatic sidecar restart with exponential backoff; if restart fails within 30s, mark instance unhealthy and remove from service discovery; traffic reroutes to healthy instances

Risk: Certificate expiration causing mTLS handshake failures across the mesh
Recovery: Proactive certificate rotation 24 hours before expiry; if rotation fails, fall back to last valid certificate with 48-hour grace period while alerting operators

Risk: Control plane outage preventing policy updates and certificate issuance
Recovery: Sidecars continue operating with last-known configuration; cached certificates remain valid; stale policy enforcement persists until control plane recovers; degrade to permissive mTLS mode

Risk: Misconfigured traffic routing causing cascading failures across services
Recovery: Validate all routing rules against a shadow traffic test before applying; automatic rollback to previous configuration if error rate exceeds 5% within 60 seconds of deployment

Risk: Observability data volume overwhelming the telemetry collection pipeline
Recovery: Adaptive sampling rate that reduces trace collection percentage when backpressure is detected; prioritize error and latency-anomaly traces over successful fast traces

Risk: Rogue service bypassing the mesh and communicating directly
Recovery: Network policies enforce that all egress from application containers routes through sidecar; iptables rules validated every 30 seconds; violation triggers alert and automatic remediation

Layer: ControlPlane
    SubLayer: ConfigDiscovery
    SubLayer: CertificateAuthority
    SubLayer: PolicyEngine
    SubLayer: TelemetryAggregator
Layer: DataPlane
    SubLayer: SidecarProxy
    SubLayer: IngressGateway
    SubLayer: EgressGateway
Layer: Observability
    SubLayer: DistributedTracing
    SubLayer: MetricsCollection
    SubLayer: LogAggregation

Validation: All sidecar proxies must present valid mTLS certificates before forwarding traffic
Validation: Routing rules must not create circular dependency chains
Validation: Circuit breaker thresholds must be defined for every service dependency
Validation: Retry budgets must not exceed 3x the original request volume
Validation: Service-level objectives must be defined for every mesh-enabled service
Validation: Certificate rotation must complete before expiry with at least 12-hour margin

# Level 2: Entities
Entity SidecarProxy
    proxyId: string
    serviceId: string
    inboundPort: integer
    outboundPort: integer
    mtlsEnabled: boolean
    certificateExpiry: datetime
    configVersion: string
    lastConfigSync: datetime
    status: string
    connectedControlPlane: string

Entity ServiceEntry
    serviceName: string
    namespace: string
    hostnames: list
    ports: list
    protocol: string
    resolution: string
    endpoints: list
    meshInternal: boolean
    healthStatus: string

Entity TrafficRule
    ruleId: string
    destinationService: string
    sourceService: string
    weight: integer
    matchConditions: list
    rewritePath: string
    requestTimeout: float
    retryPolicy: dict
    circuitBreakerConfig: dict
    priority: integer

Entity MTLSCertificate
    certificateId: string
    serviceIdentity: string
    issuer: string
    notBefore: datetime
    notAfter: datetime
    serialNumber: string
    rootCA: string
    rotationCount: integer
    trustDomain: string

Entity ObservabilityConfig

    Then open the circuit breaker, immediately reject all requests to that destination with 503, emit circuit-open event, and schedule half-open probe after cooldown period

Condition: CertificateNearExpiry

Condition: ControlPlaneDisconnected

Condition: RoutingRuleConflict

Condition: BackpressureDetected

# Level 5: Events

Event: OnTrafficShiftCompleted

Event: OnCertificateRotated

Event: OnCircuitStateChange

Event: OnPolicyViolation

    xDS configuration distribution to all sidecars
    Health checking of all mesh endpoints

# Level 7: Optimization
Optimize: Sidecar proxy latency overhead

Optimize: Control plane push efficiency

Optimize: Telemetry resource consumption
    Priority: Adaptive sampling that reduces collection under load; aggregate metrics at sidecar before export; use protobuf encoding for trace spans to minimize serialization overhead

# Level 8: Learning
Learn: Optimal circuit breaker thresholds per service
    Goal: Set circuit breaker failure thresholds that catch genuine failures without overreacting to transient errors
    Adapt: consecutiveFailureThreshold and evaluationWindow
    Based: Historical error rate patterns, time-of-day traffic variability, and downstream service recovery time distributions over the last 7 days

Learn: Optimal tracing sampling rate
    Goal: Collect enough traces for statistical significance while minimizing overhead
    Adapt: tracingSamplingRate per service
    Based: Request volume, error rate, and latency percentiles; increase sampling for anomalous patterns and decrease for stable operations

Learn: Certificate rotation timing
    Goal: Rotate certificates at the optimal time to minimize connection disruption
    Adapt: rotationWindowStart (hours before expiry)
    Based: Connection lifetime distributions, peak traffic periods, and historical rotation failure rates per service

# Level 9: Security
Security:
    Encrypt: All inter-service traffic using mTLS with SPIFFE identity verification
    Encrypt: Control plane communication using separate internal CA with mutual authentication
    Encrypt: Certificate private keys at rest using HSM-backed key management
    Protect: Sidecar proxy configuration against tampering via signed xDS payloads
    Protect: Service identities against spoofing via SPIFFE SVID validation
    Protect: Telemetry data against injection by validating traceparent headers against cryptographic spans
    Protect: Policy rules against unauthorized modification via RBAC on control plane API

# Level 10: Native
Native: Rust

use std::sync::Arc;
use tokio::net::TcpListener;
use tokio::sync::RwLock;

struct SidecarProxy {
    config: Arc<RwLock<ProxyConfig>>,
    connection_pool: ConnectionPool,
    cert_manager: CertificateManager,
    telemetry: TelemetryCollector,
    circuit_breakers: Arc<RwLock<HashMap<String, CircuitBreaker>>>,
    policy_engine: PolicyEngine,
}

impl SidecarProxy {
    async fn handle_inbound(&self, mut stream: TcpStream) -> Result<(), ProxyError> {
        let config = self.config.read().await;
        
        // Perform mTLS handshake
        let tls_stream = self.cert_manager
            .accept_with_mtls(&mut stream).await?;
        
        // Parse request headers
        let request = parse_request(tls_stream).await?;
        
        // Enforce policy
        if !self.policy_engine.evaluate(&request).await? {
            return Err(ProxyError::PolicyDenied);
        }
        
        // Check circuit breaker
        let dest = &request.destination_service;
        let breakers = self.circuit_breakers.read().await;
        if let Some(cb) = breakers.get(dest) {
            if cb.is_open() {
                return Err(ProxyError::CircuitOpen);
            }
        }
        
        // Apply routing rules
        let endpoint = config.resolve_route(&request)?;
        
        // Forward with tracing
        let span = self.telemetry.start_span("proxy-forward");
        let response = self.connection_pool
            .forward(endpoint, request).await?;
        self.telemetry.finish_span(span, &response);
        
        Ok(())
    }
    
    async fn run(&self, listener: TcpListener) -> Result<(), ProxyError> {
        loop {
            let (stream, _) = listener.accept().await?;
            let proxy = self.clone();
            tokio::spawn(async move {
                if let Err(e) = proxy.handle_inbound(stream).await {
                    proxy.telemetry.record_error(&e);
                }
            });
        }
    }
}

# AICL Example: Message Broker
# Implements a distributed message broker with topic/queue management, publish-subscribe,
# exactly-once delivery semantics, partitioning, consumer groups, and dead-letter handling.

# Level 1: Architecture
Goal: Provide a highly scalable, durable message broker that supports publish-subscribe and point-to-point messaging with exactly-once delivery semantics, ordered partition consumption, consumer group balancing, and guaranteed message persistence across node failures.

Constraint: Messages must be persisted to disk before acknowledging the producer
Constraint: Exactly-once delivery requires idempotent producer and transactional consumer
Constraint: Partition count per topic must not exceed the number of broker nodes
Constraint: Consumer group rebalancing must complete within the session timeout period
Constraint: Message ordering must be maintained within a single partition
Constraint: Retention policy must be enforced even if consumers have not consumed messages

Risk: Message loss during broker failover before disk persistence
Recovery: Synchronous replication to in-sync replicas before acknowledging producer; if primary fails, ISR member promotes with complete log; unreplicated messages are re-sent by producer with idempotent retry

Risk: Consumer group rebalancing storm causing processing halts
Recovery: Cooperative sticky assignment strategy minimizes partition movement; incremental cooperative rebalancing avoids stop-the-world pauses; rebalance throttle limits partition reassignment rate

Risk: Duplicate message delivery due to producer retry after acknowledgment
Recovery: Idempotent producer with sequence numbers per partition; broker deduplicates based on producer ID and sequence number; consumer enables transactional reads with commit-after-processing semantics

Risk: Partition leader failure causing consumer lag and unavailability
Recovery: Controller detects leader failure via ZooKeeper/RAFT session expiry; new leader elected from ISR; consumers reconnect and resume from last committed offset; unclean leader election prevented by default

Risk: Dead-letter queue overflow from poison messages
Recovery: Dead-letter queue has independent retention policy; messages exceeding max delivery attempts are moved to DLQ; DLQ monitoring triggers alert at 80% capacity; manual replay mechanism for DLQ messages

Risk: Disk exhaustion from high-throughput topics exceeding retention cleanup rate
Recovery: Enforce hard retention limit with aggressive log segment deletion; throttle producers on partitions nearing disk quota; automatic broker defragmentation; alert at 85% disk utilization

    SubLayer: PartitionManager
    SubLayer: ReplicationManager

    SubLayer: HeartbeatManager

Validation: All published messages must be persisted to at least min.insync.replicas before acknowledgment
Validation: Consumer offset commits must be atomic across all assigned partitions
Validation: Partition leader must always be a member of the in-sync replica set
Validation: Topic configuration changes must not reduce partition count
Validation: Transactional producer must not interleave transactional and non-transactional messages
Validation: Consumer group generation must monotonically increase on each rebalance

# Level 2: Entities

# Level 3: Behaviors
Behavior ProduceMessage

    Output: partition: integer, offset: integer, timestamp: datetime
    Action:
        Validate topic exists and message size within limits

        Validate consumer generation matches current group generation
        If transactional commit, validate transaction is in committing state
        Write offset commits to internal __consumer_offsets topic
        Replicate offset commit to ensure durability
        Return confirmed committed offsets
        Trigger lag metrics update

Behavior RebalanceGroup

    Output: newAssignment: dict, generationId: integer
    Action:
        Increment group generation counter
        Revoke currently assigned partitions from all members

        Minimize partition movement from previous assignment
        Distribute new assignment to all group members
        Wait for member acknowledgment within rebalance timeout

Behavior HandlePoisonMessage
    Input: topic: string, partition: integer, offset: integer, error: string, deliveryCount: integer
    Output: dlqPartition: integer, dlqOffset: integer
    Action:
        If deliveryCount exceeds max.redelivery.count, route to dead-letter topic
        Enrich message with failure metadata (reason, original partition/offset)
        Produce to DLQ topic with same key for ordering
        Commit offset past the poison message to unblock consumer

    Input: topicName: string, partitionCount: integer, replicationFactor: integer, config: dict
    Output: success: boolean, topicMetadata: dict
    Action:
        Validate topic name follows naming conventions
        Assign partition leaders and replicas across brokers using rack-aware assignment
        Create log directories on assigned brokers
        Register topic in cluster metadata
        Propagate metadata to all brokers via controller notification
        Return topic metadata including partition assignments

# Level 4: Conditions
Condition: ISRShrinksBelowMin
    When in-sync replica count for a partition drops below min.insync.replicas
    Then reject all produce requests for that partition with NOT_ENOUGH_REPLICAS error code; alert operations team; attempt to recover lagging replicas by truncating to leader's log end offset

Condition: ConsumerSessionExpired
    When consumer fails to send heartbeat within session.timeout.ms
    Then trigger group rebalance to reassign the departed consumer's partitions; mark consumer as removed; log session expiry event with consumer ID and last heartbeat timestamp

Condition: DiskUsageThreshold
    When broker disk usage exceeds retention.bytes or reaches 85% capacity
    Then aggressively delete oldest log segments; throttle producers on affected partitions; if throttling insufficient, reject new produces with POLICY_VIOLATION; alert operations

Condition: UncleanLeaderElection
    When no in-sync replica is available to become partition leader
    Then if unclean.leader.election.enable is true, elect from out-of-sync replicas with data loss warning; if false, partition remains unavailable; emit critical alert either way

Condition: TransactionTimeout
    When transactional producer fails to commit or abort within transaction.timeout.ms
    Then transaction coordinator automatically aborts the transaction; release all locked partitions; emit transaction timeout metric; subsequent produce requests from same producerId are rejected until producer recovers with new epoch

# Level 5: Events
Event: OnNewPartitionLeader
    On partition leadership changes to a new broker
    Action: Update cluster metadata, notify producers of new leader endpoint, redirect consumer fetch requests, update ISR tracking, emit leader change metric, verify new leader has complete log

Event: OnConsumerGroupRebalance
    On consumer group membership or subscription change
    Action: Pause consumption on revoked partitions, commit offsets before revocation, process new partition assignments, reset fetch positions for newly assigned partitions, emit rebalance duration metric

Event: OnMessageProduced
    On message successfully appended and replicated to partition
    Action: Update partition high watermark, emit produce latency metric, check if log segment rotation needed, trigger retention cleanup if segment size exceeds threshold, update topic bytes counter

Event: OnDLQMessageAdded
    On message moved to dead-letter queue
    Action: Emit DLQ metric with error classification, increment poison message counter, notify consumer application via callback if registered, log original offset and failure reason for debugging

Event: OnBrokerJoined
    On new broker registered with the cluster controller
    Action: Assign partition replicas to new broker for load balancing, trigger partial rebalance if auto-leader-rebalance enabled, update cluster metadata on all brokers, begin log catchup for new replicas

# Level 6: Concurrency
Parallel:
    Independent partition log append operations across leaders
    Consumer fetch requests from different groups on different partitions
    Log segment deletion and retention enforcement
    Replica fetcher threads per broker for ISR maintenance
    Offset commit processing from multiple consumer groups

# Level 7: Optimization
Optimize: Produce throughput
    Priority: Batch messages per partition using linger.ms and batch.size; compress batches with lz4/zstd; use zero-copy transfer via sendfile for replica fetching; group produce requests by destination broker

Optimize: Consumer fetch efficiency
    Priority: Implement read-ahead with predictable prefetch; batch fetch across multiple partitions; use memory-mapped index files for fast offset lookup; return data in zero-copy mode to consumer

Optimize: Log segment management
    Priority: Pre-allocate log segment files to avoid filesystem fragmentation; use sparse index files with interval-based indexing; parallelize segment deletion across topic partitions

# Level 8: Learning
Learn: Optimal partition count for throughput
    Goal: Determine the ideal partition count per topic that maximizes parallelism without excessive overhead
    Adapt: recommendedPartitionCount per topic
    Based: Producer throughput, consumer group size, and per-partition latency measurements over the last 24 hours

Learn: Optimal batch size and linger time
    Goal: Maximize throughput while keeping P99 produce latency under target
    Adapt: batchSize and lingerMs per producer
    Based: Observed produce latency distribution, message size distribution, and current throughput requirements

Learn: Consumer group rebalance strategy
    Goal: Minimize rebalance duration and processing disruption
    Adapt: sessionTimeoutMs and rebalanceTimeoutMs per group
    Based: Historical rebalance frequency, duration, and processing delay caused by stop-the-world pauses

# Level 9: Security
Security:
    Encrypt: All inter-broker communication using TLS with mutual authentication
    Encrypt: Client-to-broker connections using TLS with optional SASL authentication
    Encrypt: Message payloads at rest using AES-256 for sensitive topics
    Protect: Topic access via ACLs (produce, consume, describe, alter)
    Protect: Consumer group operations via group-level ACLs
    Protect: Administrative operations (topic creation, config change) via super-user RBAC
    Protect: Transactional IDs against hijacking via producer epoch validation

# Level 10: Native

public class PartitionLog {
    private final FileChannel logChannel;
    private final OffsetIndex offsetIndex;
    private final TimeIndex timeIndex;
    private final long rollSizeBytes;
    private volatile long logEndOffset;
    private volatile long highWatermark;
    private final ConcurrentLinkedQueue<LogSegment> segments;

    public synchronized long append(MemoryRecords records) throws IOException {
        long offset = logEndOffset;
        
        // Validate and assign offsets
        for (RecordBatch batch : records.batches()) {
            batch.setBaseOffset(offset);
            offset += batch.countOrNull() != null ? batch.countOrNull() : 1;
        }
        
        // Roll to new segment if needed
        if (activeSegment().sizeInBytes() > rollSizeBytes) {
            roll();
        }
        
        // Append to active segment
        activeSegment().append(records);
        logEndOffset = offset;
        
        // Update indices
        offsetIndex.append(logEndOffset, activeSegment().sizeInBytes());
        timeIndex.append(System.currentTimeMillis(), logEndOffset);
        
        // Flush based on flush policy
        if (flushOnWrite) {
            logChannel.force(true);
        }
        
        return logEndOffset;
    }

    public synchronized void updateHighWatermark(long newHw) {
        if (newHw >= highWatermark) {
            highWatermark = newHw;
        }
    }

    public FetchData read(long startOffset, int maxLength) {
        LogSegment segment = findSegment(startOffset);
        if (segment == null) return FetchData.empty();
        
        int position = offsetIndex.lookup(startOffset).position;
        return segment.read(position, maxLength);
    }
}
