# AICL Example: Distributed Cache
# Implements a distributed cache with consistent hashing, replication, eviction policies,
# cache invalidation, read-through/write-through patterns, and backfill strategies.

# Level 1: Architecture
Goal: Provide a low-latency, highly available distributed caching layer that supports consistent hashing for horizontal scaling, multi-region replication, configurable eviction policies, and transparent read-through/write-through integration with backend data stores.

Constraint: Cache consistency must follow eventual consistency model with configurable max staleness bound
Constraint: Consistent hashing ring must distribute keys within 10% of uniform distribution
Constraint: Replication factor must ensure data survives any single node failure
Constraint: Eviction must occur before memory usage exceeds 95% of allocated capacity
Constraint: All cache operations must complete within 5ms P99 at the local region

Risk: Cache stampede causing thundering herd on cache miss
Recovery: Implement request coalescing for in-flight key fetches; only one request per key fetches from backend; other concurrent requests wait on shared future; probabilistic early expiration to stagger re-fetches

Risk: Hotspot key overwhelming single node despite consistent hashing
Recovery: Implement virtual nodes (150+ per physical node) for better distribution; for extreme hotspots, replicate hot keys to multiple nodes using read replicas; client-side local caching for top-K hot keys

Risk: Network partition causing cache inconsistency between regions
Recovery: Version vectors track causality; conflict resolution using last-write-wins with synchronized clocks; on partition heal, anti-entropy protocol reconciles divergent entries using version comparison; tombstones for deletions

Risk: Node failure causing temporary data loss and increased backend load
Recovery: Replicated copies on adjacent ring positions serve reads; background re-replication fills new node from replicas; client retry with replica read on primary failure; circuit breaker prevents backend cascade

Risk: Memory pressure causing unpredictable eviction of recently cached data
Recovery: Segmented LRU (protected/probationary) with admission window; items must prove value before entering protected segment; dynamic pool sizing based on hit rate feedback; OOM protection via hard eviction threshold

Risk: Consistent hashing rebalancing causing massive key migration on topology change
Recovery: Use bounded loads consistent hashing to limit key movement; vnodes ensure only affected partitions move; rebalancing throttled to prevent network saturation; clients update ring topology lazily

Validation: Replication factor must be at least 2 for any write-acknowledged key
Validation: Eviction policy must protect recently admitted items from immediate re-eviction
Validation: Read-through callback must have a timeout of at most 500ms
Validation: Cache invalidation must propagate to all replicas within the consistency window
Validation: Memory usage must not exceed 95% before triggering proactive eviction

# Level 3: Behaviors
Behavior GetEntry
    Input: key: string, consistencyLevel: string, timeoutMs: integer
    Output: value: bytes, version: integer, hit: boolean, sourceNode: string
    Action:
        Hash key to locate primary node on the ring
        If local hit, return value from storage engine
        If miss, check replica nodes based on consistency level
        If read-through enabled, coalesce with in-flight fetches for same key
        Fetch from backend if all cache nodes miss; store result on primary
        Apply TTL check and return stale-if-valid if within grace period

    Output: version: integer, replicatedNodes: list, latencyMs: float
    Action:
        Hash key to determine primary and replica nodes
        Check admission policy before accepting entry
        Write to primary node storage engine
        Replicate to N-1 replica nodes based on replication factor
        Await write quorum acknowledgment before responding

        Determine all nodes holding the key or keys matching pattern

        If synchronous, await acknowledgment from all target nodes
        If asynchronous, fire-and-forget with best-effort delivery

    Action:
        Compute new ring topology with virtual node assignments
        Identify keys that must migrate to new primary nodes
        Transfer key ranges to new owners with streaming
        Verify data integrity on destination nodes

        Throttle migration rate to avoid impacting production traffic

Behavior EvictEntries
    Input: targetMemoryBytes: integer, policy: EvictionPolicy
    Output: evictedCount: integer, freedBytes: integer
    Action:
        Scan probationary segment of segmented LRU first
        Apply admission filter to protect frequently accessed items
        If probationary insufficient, evict from protected segment's tail
        Respect TTL-based expiration before policy-based eviction
        Update hit rate metrics after each eviction batch
        Dynamically adjust protected/probationary ratio based on hit rate
        Emit eviction count and memory metrics

Behavior ResolveConflict
    Input: key: string, localEntry: CacheEntry, remoteEntry: CacheEntry
    Output: resolvedEntry: CacheEntry, resolution: string
    Action:
        Compare version vectors for causal ordering
        If one version dominates, use that entry as resolved
        If concurrent versions, apply conflict resolution strategy
        For last-write-wins, compare timestamps from synchronized clocks
        For merge, combine non-overlapping fields if applicable
        Write resolved entry and propagate anti-entropy update
        Log conflict for analysis of consistency model violations

# Level 4: Conditions
Condition: MemoryThresholdBreached
    When cache node memory usage exceeds 90% of allocated capacity
    Then trigger proactive eviction of probationary tier entries; if insufficient, evict from protected tier; throttle new admissions until usage drops below 85%; emit critical memory metric

Condition: ReplicationLagExceeded
    When replica falls behind primary by more than replicationLagThresholdMs
    Then mark replica as stale for read quorum calculations; redirect reads to healthy replicas; trigger catchup replication stream; if catchup fails within 5 minutes, mark replica as degraded

Condition: ConsistentHashImbalance
    When any node's key count deviates more than 15% from the average
    Then redistribute virtual nodes to balance load; consider adding virtual nodes to underloaded physical nodes; emit imbalance metric; trigger background rebalancing

Condition: BackendUnreachable
    When read-through or write-through backend becomes unreachable
    Then serve stale cache entries beyond TTL within grace period; queue write-through writes for async backend delivery; circuit break backend calls after 5 consecutive failures; emit backend unavailability alert

Condition: StampedeDetected
    When more than 10 concurrent requests miss the same key within 100ms
    Then coalesce all requests into single backend fetch; return shared future result to all waiters; implement probabilistic early expiration (PER) to stagger future re-fetches; emit stampede metric

# Level 5: Events
Event: OnNodeJoined
    On new cache node added to the cluster
    Action: Register node on hash ring, assign virtual nodes, begin key migration from overloaded neighbors, update client routing tables, start replication streams, emit node-join metric

Event: OnNodeFailed
    On cache node declared failed after missing heartbeats
    Action: Remove from hash ring, promote replicas to primary for affected keys, trigger re-replication to restore replication factor, update client routing tables, begin data recovery from remaining replicas

Event: OnCacheHitRateDrop
    On global cache hit rate drops below configured target for 5 consecutive minutes
    Action: Analyze eviction patterns, increase protected segment ratio, adjust admission policy, identify churn patterns, consider increasing cache capacity, emit hit rate degradation alert

Event: OnInvalidationBroadcast
    On invalidation message received from another region
    Action: Apply invalidation to local storage, acknowledge if synchronous, update version vector, propagate to any downstream replicas, emit cross-region invalidation metric

Event: OnRebalanceComplete
    On ring rebalancing migration finishes
    Action: Verify all key ranges are correctly placed, update global routing table, validate replication factor for all keys, emit rebalance completion metric with migration stats, enable full traffic on new nodes

# Level 6: Concurrency
Parallel:
    Independent cache get/put operations across different key partitions
    Background replication streams to replica nodes
    Anti-entropy reconciliation between regions
    Eviction scanning and memory management
    Client routing table updates

# Level 7: Optimization
Optimize: Cache hit rate
    Priority: Use segmented LRU with dynamic admission policy; implement probabilistic early expiration to prevent stampedes; prefetch keys with predictable access patterns; adjust protected/probationary ratio based on real-time hit rate

Optimize: Replication throughput
    Priority: Batch replication updates into pipeline messages; use async replication for non-critical consistency levels; compress replication payloads with lz4; parallelize replication to independent replicas

Optimize: Memory utilization
    Priority: Use slab allocation for common value sizes; compress cold entries with zstd; implement object pooling for cache entry metadata; memory-mapped storage for items exceeding threshold size

# Level 8: Learning
Learn: Optimal TTL for different key patterns
    Goal: Maximize hit rate while minimizing stale data served
    Adapt: default TTL per key prefix pattern
    Based: Access frequency, backend update frequency, and staleness tolerance observed over 7-day windows

Learn: Admission policy thresholds
    Goal: Prevent cache pollution from one-time access keys while retaining valuable entries
    Adapt: admissionWindow and minimumAccessCount for protected tier
    Based: Historical eviction patterns showing recently-evicted items being re-requested vs. truly cold items

Learn: Replication factor per key namespace
    Goal: Use higher replication for hot keys and lower replication for cold keys to optimize memory
    Adapt: dynamicReplicationFactor per key namespace
    Based: Access frequency distribution, read quorum requirements, and node failure probability

# Level 9: Security
Security:
    Encrypt: All inter-node replication traffic using TLS 1.3
    Encrypt: Client-to-cache connections using TLS with SASL authentication
    Encrypt: Cache entry values at rest using AES-256-GCM for sensitive key prefixes
    Protect: Key-level access control via ACLs (read, write, admin)
    Protect: Admin operations (flush, rebalance, config change) via RBAC
    Protect: Against cache poisoning by validating write authorization per namespace
    Protect: Against side-channel attacks via constant-time key comparison for authentication

{
class ConsistentHashRing {
    std::map<uint64_t, std::string> ring_;
    std::unordered_map<std::string, std::vector<uint64_t>> vnodes_;
    int replication_factor_;
    int vnodes_per_node_;
    
public:
    void addNode(const std::string& node_id) {
        std::hash<std::string> hasher;
        for (int i = 0; i < vnodes_per_node_; ++i) {
            std::string vnode_key = node_id + ":" + std::to_string(i);
            uint64_t hash = hasher(vnode_key);
            ring_[hash] = node_id;
            vnodes_[node_id].push_back(hash);
        }
    }

    void removeNode(const std::string& node_id) {
        for (uint64_t hash : vnodes_[node_id]) {
            ring_.erase(hash);
        }
        vnodes_.erase(node_id);
    }

    std::vector<std::string> getNodes(const std::string& key) {
        std::vector<std::string> nodes;
        if (ring_.empty()) return nodes;
        
        std::hash<std::string> hasher;
        uint64_t hash = hasher(key);
        auto it = ring_.lower_bound(hash);
        if (it == ring_.end()) it = ring_.begin();
        
        std::set<std::string> seen;
        for (int i = 0; i < replication_factor_ && seen.size() < (size_t)replication_factor_; ++i) {
            if (seen.find(it->second) == seen.end()) {
                nodes.push_back(it->second);
                seen.insert(it->second);
            }
            ++it;
            if (it == ring_.end()) it = ring_.begin();
        }
        return nodes;
    }
};

class SegmentedLRU {
    struct Entry {
        std::string key;
        std::vector<uint8_t> value;
        uint64_t version;
        std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point expire_at;
        size_t access_count;
        int tier; // 0=probationary, 1=protected
    };
    
    std::list<Entry> protected_;
    std::list<Entry> probationary_;
    std::unordered_map<std::string, std::list<Entry>::iterator> index_;
    size_t protected_capacity_;
    size_t probationary_capacity_;
    
public:
    std::optional<Entry> get(const std::string& key) {
        auto it = index_.find(key);
        if (it == index_.end()) return std::nullopt;
        
        Entry& e = *(it->second);
        if (std::chrono::steady_clock::now() > e.expire_at) {
            erase(key);
            return std::nullopt;
        }
        
        e.access_count++;
        if (e.tier == 0 && e.access_count > 1) {
            promote(it->second);
        }
        return e;
    }
    
    void promote(std::list<Entry>::iterator it) {
        Entry e = std::move(*it);
        e.tier = 1;
        probationary_.erase(it);
        
        while (protected_.size() >= protected_capacity_) {
            Entry victim = std::move(protected_.back());
            victim.tier = 0;
            victim.access_count = 1;
            protected_.pop_back();
            probationary_.push_front(std::move(victim));
            index_[probationary_.front().key] = probationary_.begin();
        }
        
        protected_.push_front(std::move(e));
        index_[protected_.front().key] = protected_.begin();
    }
};

# AICL Example: CDN System
# Implements a Content Delivery Network with edge caching, origin shielding, cache purging,
# geo-routing, DDoS mitigation, and real-time analytics for content optimization.

# Level 1: Architecture
Goal: Provide a globally distributed content delivery network that minimizes latency for end users through intelligent edge caching, origin shielding to reduce origin load, geo-based request routing, proactive cache purging, and multi-layer DDoS mitigation.

Constraint: Edge cache must serve content within 50ms of user request for cached objects
Constraint: Origin shielding layer must absorb at least 95% of requests that miss edge caches
Constraint: Cache purging must propagate to all edge locations within 30 seconds
Constraint: Geo-routing must direct users to the nearest healthy edge with less than 10ms DNS resolution
Constraint: DDoS mitigation must absorb attacks up to 10Tbps without degrading legitimate traffic

Risk: Cache poisoning through manipulated request headers or URL parameters
Recovery: Normalize all request URLs and headers before cache key computation; validate Vary headers strictly; implement cache key canonicalization; require signed URLs for sensitive content

Risk: Origin overload during cache stampede when popular content expires simultaneously
Recovery: Implement request coalescing at shield layer; staggered TTL jitter (±10%) to prevent synchronized expiration; serve stale content while async refreshing; origin connection pooling with queue depth limits

Risk: DDoS attack overwhelming edge locations with volumetric traffic
Recovery: Multi-layer mitigation — L3/L4 at network edge with BGP blackholing, L7 at application layer with rate limiting and CAPTCHA; traffic scrubbing centers for sustained attacks; auto-scaling edge capacity

Risk: Cache purging race condition serving stale content after purge command
Recovery: Implement purge confirmation with quorum acknowledgment from edge nodes; serve stale content with max-age=0 during purge propagation; use versioned URLs as alternative to purge dependency

Risk: Split-brain in geo-routing due to DNS propagation delays across resolvers
Recovery: Use anycast routing as primary with DNS as fallback; short TTL on geo-DNS records (30s); health check driven routing updates; client-side retry with alternative edge on failure

Risk: Origin failure causing complete service outage for uncached content
Recovery: Origin shielding with persistent connections and failover origins; serve stale-while-revalidate beyond TTL; maintain static snapshot of origin content for emergency serving; multi-origin configuration

    Action:

# Level 4: Conditions
Condition: EdgeCacheFull
    When edge node cache storage exceeds 90% capacity
    Then trigger aggressive eviction of least-recently-used content; skip caching of responses with short TTL; emit cache pressure metric; consider expanding storage or redistributing load

Condition: OriginUnhealthy
    When origin fails health checks for 3 consecutive intervals
    Then mark origin as down; route all requests to shield cache; serve stale-while-revalidate content beyond TTL; failover to secondary origin if configured; emit origin down alert

Condition: DDosThresholdExceeded
    When incoming request rate exceeds 10x baseline for the edge location
    Then activate DDoS mitigation rules; divert traffic through scrubbing; implement CAPTCHA for suspicious sources; scale edge capacity automatically; notify security team

Condition: PurgePropagationTimeout
    When purge acknowledgment not received from all target nodes within 30 seconds
    Then mark purge as partially complete; retry unacknowledged nodes with exponential backoff; serve stale content with must-revalidate directive on lagging nodes; emit purge timeout metric

Condition: StaleContentServedTooLong
    When content served beyond stale-while-revalidate window exceeds 5 minutes
    Then force synchronous origin fetch; invalidate the cache entry; emit staleness violation alert; investigate origin connectivity; consider failover origin

# Level 5: Events
Event: OnCacheHit
    On content served from edge cache without origin contact
    Action: Increment hit counter for cache key, update last-served timestamp, check if content approaching TTL expiry, trigger async revalidation if within stale-while-revalidate window, emit hit metric with content type

Event: OnDDoSAttackDetected
    On traffic pattern classified as DDoS attack
    Action: Activate automated mitigation rules, scale edge capacity, notify security operations center, begin traffic capture for forensic analysis, switch to aggressive rate limiting, emit attack severity metric

Event: OnOriginFailover

Event: OnPurgeComplete

Event: OnGeoRouteChange

# Level 6: Concurrency
Parallel:
    Content serving at edge nodes across global locations
    Cache purge propagation to all target nodes
    DDoS mitigation rule evaluation per request
    Origin health checking across all configured origins
    Analytics data aggregation from all edge locations
    Prefetch content distribution to edge nodes

# Level 7: Optimization
Optimize: Cache hit ratio
    Priority: Implement predictive prefetching based on access patterns; use varied TTLs with jitter to prevent synchronized expiry; optimize cache key design to maximize reuse; tiered caching with edge and shield layers

Optimize: Time-to-first-byte
    Priority: Pre-warm connections to origins; use HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 for multiplexed requests; compress content with brotli at edge; use early hints (103) for resource preloading

Optimize: Purge propagation speed
    Priority: Use gossip protocol for fast purge dissemination; batch related purge requests; implement hierarchical purge from shield to edges; use persistent connections for purge notifications

# Level 8: Learning
Learn: Optimal TTL per content type
    Goal: Maximize cache hit rate while minimizing stale content delivery
    Adapt: default TTL per content type and URL pattern
    Based: Content update frequency, origin change detection rate, and user freshness requirements observed over 30-day windows

Learn: Predictive prefetch targets
    Goal: Prefetch content that will be requested before it actually is, increasing hit rate
    Adapt: prefetchCandidateList per edge region
    Based: Sequential URL access patterns, time-of-day traffic patterns, and content popularity trends

Learn: DDoS baseline calibration
    Goal: Distinguish attack traffic from legitimate traffic spikes with minimal false positives
    Adapt: rateLimitThreshold per source pattern and time window
    Based: Historical traffic patterns, seasonal variations, and false positive/negative rates from past mitigations

# Level 9: Security
Security:
    Encrypt: All client-to-edge connections using TLS 1.3 with HSTS enforcement
    Encrypt: All edge-to-origin connections using TLS with certificate pinning
    Encrypt: Purge API communication using mTLS with API key authentication
    Protect: Against cache poisoning by strict normalization of cache keys and Vary header handling
    Protect: Against DDoS by multi-layer volumetric and application-layer mitigation
    Protect: Origin IP addresses from disclosure via shield layer abstraction
    Protect: Against request smuggling by validating Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding consistency

package cdn

import (
    "crypto/sha256"
    "net/http"
    "strings"
    "sync"
    "time"
)

type EdgeCache struct {
    store       map[string]*CacheEntry
    mu          sync.RWMutex
    maxSize     int64
    currentSize int64
    shield      *ShieldLayer
    ddos        *DDoSMitigator
    geoRouter   *GeoRouter
}

type CacheEntry struct {
    Key         string
    Content     []byte
    ContentType string
    ETag        string
    ExpiresAt   time.Time
    StaleUntil  time.Time
    HitCount    int64
    LastServed  time.Time
}

func (ec *EdgeCache) ServeHTTP(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    // DDoS check
    if ec.ddos.ShouldBlock(r) {
        w.WriteHeader(http.StatusTooManyRequests)
        return
    }
    
    cacheKey := ec.normalizeKey(r.URL.String(), r.Header)
    
    ec.mu.RLock()
    entry, ok := ec.store[cacheKey]
    ec.mu.RUnlock()
    
    if ok && time.Now().Before(entry.ExpiresAt) {
        // Cache HIT
        w.Header().Set("X-Cache", "HIT")
        w.Header().Set("ETag", entry.ETag)
        w.Header().Set("Content-Type", entry.ContentType)
        w.Write(entry.Content)
        
        entry.HitCount++
        entry.LastServed = time.Now()
        
        // Async revalidation if in stale window
        if time.Now().After(entry.StaleUntil) {
            go ec.asyncRevalidate(cacheKey, r)
        }
        return
    }
    
    // Cache MISS - try shield layer
    if entry, err := ec.shield.Fetch(cacheKey, r); err == nil {
        ec.mu.Lock()
        ec.store[cacheKey] = entry
        ec.currentSize += int64(len(entry.Content))
        ec.mu.Unlock()
        
        w.Header().Set("X-Cache", "MISS-SHIELD")
        w.Header().Set("ETag", entry.ETag)
        w.Write(entry.Content)
        return
    }
    
    // Shield MISS - fetch from origin
    resp, err := ec.fetchOrigin(r)
    if err != nil {
        // Serve stale if available
        if ok {
            w.Header().Set("X-Cache", "STALE")
            w.Write(entry.Content)
            return
        }
        http.Error(w, "Origin unavailable", http.StatusBadGateway)
        return
    }
    defer resp.Body.Close()
    
    // Cache and serve origin response
    newEntry := ec.buildEntry(cacheKey, resp)
    ec.mu.Lock()
    ec.store[cacheKey] = newEntry
    ec.evictIfNeeded()
    ec.mu.Unlock()
    
    w.Header().Set("X-Cache", "MISS")
    w.Header().Set("ETag", newEntry.ETag)
    w.Write(newEntry.Content)
}

func (ec *EdgeCache) normalizeKey(url string, headers http.Header) string {
    normalized := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(url))
    h := sha256.New()
    h.Write([]byte(normalized))
    varyHeaders := headers.Get("Vary")
    if varyHeaders != "" {
        for _, vh := range strings.Split(varyHeaders, ",") {
            h.Write([]byte(headers.Get(strings.TrimSpace(vh))))
        }
    }
    return string(h.Sum(nil))
}

# AICL Example: Load Balancer
# Implements a Layer 4/Layer 7 load balancer with health checking, session affinity,
# rate limiting, SSL termination, connection draining, and adaptive routing algorithms.

# Level 1: Architecture
Goal: Provide a high-performance load balancer that distributes traffic across backend pools at both L4 (TCP/UDP) and L7 (HTTP/gRPC) layers, with intelligent health checking, session persistence, request-level rate limiting, SSL/TLS termination, and graceful connection draining during backend changes.

Constraint: Health check intervals must not exceed 10 seconds for critical services
Constraint: Session affinity must guarantee sticky routing for the duration of a session timeout
Constraint: Rate limiting must enforce per-client quotas with at most 1% overshoot under burst conditions
Constraint: SSL termination must not add more than 1ms to connection establishment time
Constraint: Backend pool changes must propagate within 5 seconds to all load balancer instances

Risk: All backends in a pool becoming unhealthy simultaneously
Recovery: Enable circuit breaker with fallback response (cached content or custom error page); continue health checking at accelerated interval (2s); auto-scale backend pool if integrated with orchestrator; alert operations with critical severity

Risk: Uneven load distribution due to session affinity override of balancing algorithm
Recovery: Monitor per-backend load deviation; when imbalance exceeds 20%, implement affinity rebalancing by migrating sessions to underloaded backends; use consistent hashing with bounded loads to limit maximum per-backend load

Risk: SSL certificate expiry causing TLS handshake failures
Recovery: Automated certificate management with ACME protocol; rotate certificates 30 days before expiry; hot-reload certificates without dropping active connections; pin alert on 60-day expiry threshold

Risk: Rate limiter state divergence across multiple load balancer instances
Recovery: Implement distributed rate limiting with sliding window counters replicated via consistent hashing; use atomic increment operations on shared counters; accept eventual consistency with 1-second convergence window

Risk: Connection draining timeout during rolling deployment causing request loss
Recovery: Configure generous drain timeout (300s default); send GOAWAY frame for HTTP/2 connections; respect Connection: close for HTTP/1.1; queue in-flight requests for completion before backend removal; force-kill only after drain timeout

Risk: Hot path performance degradation from excessive L7 inspection
Recovery: Offload health checks and metrics to dedicated threads; use zero-copy packet processing for L4; implement fast-path for known-good traffic patterns; sample-based deep inspection at 1% for anomaly detection

    windowSize: integer
    action: string
    scope: string
    enabled: boolean
    currentCount: integer

Entity SessionAffinityConfig
    affinityType: string
    cookieName: string
    cookieTtl: integer
    hashKey: string
    fallbackPolicy: string
    consistentHashing: boolean
    replicationFactor: integer

Entity HealthCheck
    checkId: string
    targetType: string
    intervalSeconds: integer
    timeoutSeconds: float
    healthyThreshold: integer
    unhealthyThreshold: integer
    httpPath: string
    expectedStatus: list
    expectedBody: string
    lastResult: string

# Level 3: Behaviors
Behavior RouteL4Request
    Input: sourceIp: string, sourcePort: integer, destinationPort: integer, protocol: string
    Output: backendHost: string, backendPort: integer, connectionId: string
    Action:
        Select backend pool matching destination port and protocol
        Check session affinity for existing binding
        If no affinity, select backend using configured algorithm (round-robin, least-conn, weighted)
        Verify backend is in healthy state
        Establish TCP proxy connection with zero-copy splice
        Track active connection count on selected backend
        Return backend endpoint and connection identifier

Behavior RouteL7Request
    Input: headers: dict, body: bytes, method: string, path: string, host: string
    Output: response: bytes, statusCode: integer, backendId: string, latency: float
    Action:
        Match request to routing rule based on host and path patterns
        Evaluate rate limits for client identity before routing
        Apply path rewriting rules if configured
        Select backend from pool using L7-aware algorithm
        Inject tracing headers (X-Request-Id, X-B3-TraceId)
        Proxy request with connection pooling and keep-alive
        Track response latency and error status for passive health checking
        Return response with routing metadata

Behavior PerformHealthCheck
    Input: backend: Backend, checkConfig: HealthCheck
    Output: healthy: boolean, responseTime: float, details: string
    Action:
        Execute active health check (TCP connect or HTTP GET)
        Measure response time against timeout threshold
        Validate response status code and body content
        Update consecutive success/failure counters
        If threshold crossed, transition backend health status
        If newly unhealthy, remove from active rotation immediately
        If newly healthy after recovery, add back to rotation with slow ramp-up
        Emit health check result metric

Behavior EnforceRateLimit
    Input: clientId: string, key: string, tokens: integer
    Output: allowed: boolean, remainingTokens: integer, retryAfterMs: integer
    Action:
        Compute rate limit key from client identity and rule pattern
        Increment sliding window counter for the current time bucket
        Check if counter exceeds requests-per-second threshold
        If burst allowed, consume from burst token bucket
        If rejected, compute retry-after duration from window reset
        Return allow/deny with remaining capacity and retry timing
        Emit rate limit metric with allow/deny classification

Behavior TerminateSSL
    Input: rawConnection: any, sniHostname: string
    Output: tlsConnection: any, negotiatedProtocol: string, peerCertificate: dict
    Action:
        Perform TLS handshake with SNI-based certificate selection
        Validate client certificate if mutual TLS is configured
        Select optimal cipher suite from configured preferences
        Enable OCSP stapling for certificate status verification
        Negotiate ALPN protocol (h2, http/1.1)
        Establish decrypted connection for L7 processing
        Track TLS handshake latency metric

Behavior DrainBackend
    Input: backendId: string, timeoutSeconds: integer, drainReason: string
    Output: drainedConnections: integer, timedOut: boolean
    Action:
        Mark backend as draining in pool configuration
        Stop routing new connections to the draining backend
        Send GOAWAY frame for HTTP/2 connections on the backend
        Wait for in-flight requests to complete up to timeout
        Track remaining active connections during drain
        If timeout expires, forcefully terminate remaining connections
        Remove backend from pool after drain completes
        Emit drain completion metric with connection count

# Level 4: Conditions
Condition: BackendUnhealthyThreshold
    When consecutive failed health checks exceed unhealthy threshold for a backend
    Then immediately remove backend from active rotation; distribute its load across remaining healthy backends; begin checking at accelerated interval; trigger backend recovery alert

Condition: PoolCapacityCritical
    When healthy backend count drops below 50% of total pool size
    Then activate circuit breaker with custom fallback response; alert operations with critical severity; trigger auto-scaling if available; reduce rate limits to protect remaining backends

Condition: RateLimitExceeded
    When client request rate exceeds configured threshold for the rate limit rule
    Then return HTTP 429 with Retry-After header; log rate limit event with client identity; if sustained abuse, add to temporary block list; emit rate limit metric

Condition: SSLHandshakeFailure
    When TLS handshake fails due to certificate validation, protocol mismatch, or cipher negotiation
    Then log handshake failure with reason code; emit TLS error metric; if client certificate required, return appropriate TLS alert; do not fall back to insecure protocols

Condition: BackendLatencyAnomaly
    When backend P99 latency exceeds 3x the pool average for 2 consecutive check intervals
    Then mark backend as degraded with reduced weight; redirect new sessions to healthier backends; trigger passive outlier detection; if latency persists, remove from rotation

# Level 5: Events
Event: OnBackendAdded
    On new backend registered to a pool
    Action: Begin health checking with ramp-up period, gradually increase weight from 10% to 100% over 5 minutes, establish connection pool warm-up, emit backend-add metric, update routing table

Event: OnBackendRemoved
    On backend removed from pool (planned or unplanned)
    Action: Initiate connection draining if planned, redistribute sessions immediately if unplanned, update pool configuration, emit backend-removal metric, verify remaining pool capacity

Event: OnSSLExpiryWarning
    On SSL certificate within 30 days of expiration
    Action: Trigger automated ACME renewal, alert operations team, verify renewal succeeds, hot-reload new certificate, emit certificate-expiry-warning metric

Event: OnRateLimitTriggered
    On rate limit rule denies a request
    Action: Return 429 response with Retry-After, log client identity and rule, emit rate-limit-denied metric, check if pattern indicates abuse, consider temporary block for persistent abusers

Event: OnCircuitBreakerOpen
    On circuit breaker opens for a backend pool
    Action: Serve fallback response to all requests, emit circuit-open metric with reason, alert operations, begin probe requests at reduced rate, auto-close circuit when probes succeed

# Level 6: Concurrency
Parallel:
    L4 TCP proxy connections with zero-copy splice
    L7 HTTP request routing with connection pooling
    Health checking across all backends at configured intervals
    SSL/TLS handshakes on incoming connections
    Rate limit counter updates across distributed state
    Metrics aggregation and export

# Level 7: Optimization
Optimize: Request routing latency
    Priority: Use connection pooling with keep-alive to backends; pre-warm connections; implement LRU cache for routing rule lookups; use RCU-optimized data structures for pool membership

Optimize: SSL termination throughput
    Priority: Use hardware acceleration (AES-NI) for cipher operations; enable TLS session resumption and tickets; batch TLS handshakes; use OCSP stapling to reduce client verification round trips

Optimize: Health check efficiency
    Priority: Parallelize health checks across backends; use passive health checking from real traffic; implement adaptive intervals (faster when unhealthy, slower when stable); batch health check results

# Level 8: Learning
Learn: Optimal balancing algorithm per pool
    Goal: Automatically select the best load balancing algorithm based on traffic patterns
    Adapt: balancingAlgorithm per backend pool
    Based: Request latency distribution, backend capacity heterogeneity, and session affinity requirements observed over 24-hour windows

Learn: Rate limit thresholds
    Goal: Set rate limits that protect backends without blocking legitimate traffic spikes
    Adapt: requestsPerSecond and burstSize per client tier
    Based: Historical traffic patterns, false positive rates, and backend saturation indicators

Learn: Health check timing
    Goal: Detect failures quickly without overwhelming backends with health check traffic
    Adapt: healthCheckInterval and thresholds per pool
    Based: Backend failure patterns (gradual degradation vs. sudden failure), time to detect failures, and health check overhead

# Level 9: Security
Security:
    Encrypt: All client-to-load-balancer connections using TLS 1.3 with strong cipher suites
    Encrypt: Load-balancer-to-backend connections using mTLS or IPsec tunnels
    Encrypt: Rate limit state synchronization between LB instances
    Protect: Against DDoS with connection rate limiting and syn-cookie protection
    Protect: Against HTTP request smuggling with Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding validation
    Protect: Backend endpoints from direct access via network ACLs
    Protect: SSL private keys using HSM or sealed secrets with restricted access

# Level 10: Native
Native: C
{
#include <sys/epoll.h>
#include <netinet/in.h>
#include <openssl/ssl.h>
#include <openssl/err.h>

typedef struct {
    int fd;
    SSL *ssl;
    int backend_fd;
    int state;
    time_t last_active;
} connection_t;

typedef struct {
    char host[256];
    int port;
    int weight;
    int active_conns;
    int healthy;
    time_t last_check;
    double latency_p99;
} backend_t;

typedef struct {
    backend_t *backends;
    int backend_count;
    int rr_index;
    int epoll_fd;
    SSL_CTX *ssl_ctx;
    connection_t *connections;
    int max_connections;
} lb_state_t;

static backend_t *select_backend(lb_state_t *lb, const char *affinity_key) {
    // Least connections with weight consideration
    backend_t *best = NULL;
    double best_score = 1e9;
    
    for (int i = 0; i < lb->backend_count; i++) {
        backend_t *b = &lb->backends[i];
        if (!b->healthy) continue;
        
        double score = (double)b->active_conns / (double)b->weight;
        if (score < best_score) {
            best_score = score;
            best = b;
        }
    }
    return best;
}

static void handle_client_data(lb_state_t *lb, connection_t *conn) {
    char buf[65536];
    int n = SSL_read(conn->ssl, buf, sizeof(buf));
    if (n <= 0) {
        close_connection(lb, conn);
        return;
    }
    
    // Zero-copy splice for TCP proxy mode
    ssize_t sent = send(conn->backend_fd, buf, n, MSG_NOSIGNAL);
    if (sent != n) {
        close_connection(lb, conn);
    }
}

static void accept_connection(lb_state_t *lb, int listen_fd) {
    struct sockaddr_in addr;
    socklen_t len = sizeof(addr);
    int client_fd = accept(listen_fd, (struct sockaddr*)&addr, &len);
    if (client_fd < 0) return;
    
    SSL *ssl = SSL_new(lb->ssl_ctx);
    SSL_set_fd(ssl, client_fd);
    
    if (SSL_accept(ssl) <= 0) {
        SSL_free(ssl);
        close(client_fd);
        return;
    }
    
    backend_t *backend = select_backend(lb, NULL);
    if (!backend) {
        SSL_free(ssl);
        close(client_fd);
        return;
    }
    
    int backend_fd = connect_to_backend(backend);
    if (backend_fd < 0) {
        SSL_free(ssl);
        close(client_fd);
        return;
    }
    
    connection_t *conn = &lb->connections[client_fd];
    conn->fd = client_fd;
    conn->ssl = ssl;
    conn->backend_fd = backend_fd;
    conn->state = CONN_ACTIVE;
    conn->last_active = time(NULL);
    
    backend->active_conns++;
    
    struct epoll_event ev;
    ev.events = EPOLLIN | EPOLLET;
    ev.data.fd = client_fd;
    epoll_ctl(lb->epoll_fd, EPOLL_CTL_ADD, client_fd, &ev);
}

title: Service Registry & Discovery
description: AICL Example: Service Registry & Discovery Implements a service registry with health checking, DNS integration, metadata management, watch/notify pattern, multi-datacenter replication, and consistent service catalog.
instruction: Create an AICL specification for a service registry & discovery. Include all 10 language levels: architecture (goals, constraints, risks with recovery, layers), entities, behaviors, conditions, events, concurrency, optimization, learning, security, and native code.
completion:
# AICL Example: Service Registry & Discovery
# Implements a service registry with health checking, DNS integration, metadata management,
# watch/notify pattern, multi-datacenter replication, and consistent service catalog.

# Level 1: Architecture
Goal: Provide a highly available service registry and discovery system that enables dynamic service registration, real-time health checking, DNS-based and API-based service lookup, watch/notify for configuration changes, and multi-datacenter replication for global service visibility.

Constraint: Service registration must be confirmed within 2 seconds across all registry nodes
Constraint: Health check status changes must propagate within 5 seconds to all watchers
Constraint: DNS queries must resolve within 10ms for locally cached service records
Constraint: Registry must maintain availability during any single datacenter outage
Conflict: Eventual consistency between datacenters; strong consistency within a single datacenter
Constraint: Service metadata updates must be versioned with optimistic concurrency control

Risk: Service registration loss during registry node failure
Recovery: Replicate registration data across quorum of nodes; if primary fails, follower promotes with complete state; clients re-register on transient failures with deduplication; tombstone cleanup for expired registrations

Risk: Stale health check status causing traffic routing to dead instances
Recovery: Implement both active and passive health checking; deregister services after 3 consecutive check failures; watchers receive deregistration events; circuit breakers in consumers catch stale endpoints

Risk: Split-brain between datacenters causing divergent service catalogs
Recovery: Use last-write-wins with vector clocks for conflict resolution; on reconnection, anti-entropy sync reconciles divergent state; manual merge UI for unresolved conflicts; prefer datacenter with more recent writes

Risk: Watch notification storm from bulk service changes
Recovery: Batch watch notifications within 100ms window; rate limit notifications per watcher; use snapshot + delta pattern for initial state transfer; exponential backoff on watch reconnection

Risk: DNS cache poisoning serving incorrect service endpoints
Recovery: DNSSEC signing of all service records; short TTL (10s) for dynamic services; validate DNS responses against API query results; TLS for DNS-over-HTTPS lookups

Risk: Metadata schema evolution causing deserialization failures
Recovery: Schema registry with backward-compatible versioning; unknown fields preserved but not interpreted; graceful degradation for missing fields; metadata validation on write

Layer: RegistryCore
    SubLayer: RegistrationStore
    SubLayer: HealthCheckEngine
    SubLayer: WatchManager
    SubLayer: ReplicationManager
Layer: DiscoveryAPI
    SubLayer: DNSResolver
    SubLayer: HTTPAPI
    SubLayer: gRPCAPI
Layer: MultiDC
    SubLayer: CrossDCReplication
    SubLayer: ConflictResolver
    SubLayer: GlobalCatalog

Validation: Service IDs must be globally unique across all datacenters
Validation: Health check definitions must include timeout and interval specifications
Validation: Watch subscriptions must have explicit heartbeat keep-alive mechanism
Validation: DNS records must respect TTL boundaries and never serve expired health-failed endpoints
Validation: Cross-DC replication lag must not exceed 30 seconds under normal conditions
Validation: Service metadata must pass schema validation before persistence

# Level 2: Entities
Entity ServiceRegistration
    serviceId: string
    serviceName: string
    version: string
    host: string
    port: integer
    protocol: string
    metadata: dict
    tags: list
    datacenter: string
    registeredAt: datetime
    ttlSeconds: integer
    healthStatus: string

Entity HealthCheckDefinition
    checkId: string
    serviceId: string
    checkType: string
    intervalSeconds: integer
    timeoutSeconds: float
    httpPath: string
    grpcService: string
    tcpPort: integer
    deregisterAfter: integer
    successThreshold: integer
    failureThreshold: integer

Entity WatchSubscription
    watchId: string
    watcherId: string
    serviceName: string
    tagFilter: list
    datacenterFilter: list
    lastEventIndex: integer
    createdAt: datetime
    heartbeatInterval: integer
    active: boolean
    notificationEndpoint: string

Entity DNSRecord
    recordType: string
    serviceName: string
    domain: string
    ttl: integer
    endpoints: list
    healthFiltered: boolean
    lastUpdated: datetime
    weight: integer
    priority: integer

Entity DatacenterConfig
    datacenterName: string
    region: string
    apiEndpoint: string
    replicationLagMs: integer
    isConnected: boolean
    lastSyncTime: datetime
    syncVersion: integer
    peerDatacenters: list

Entity ReplicationEntry
    entryId: string
    operation: string
    serviceId: string
    datacenter: string
    vectorClock: dict
    timestamp: datetime
    payload: bytes
    acknowledged: boolean
    conflictDetected: boolean

# Level 3: Behaviors
Behavior RegisterService
    Input: serviceName: string, host: string, port: integer, metadata: dict, tags: list, ttlSeconds: integer
    Output: serviceId: string, registrationVersion: integer
    Action:
        Generate unique service ID if not provided
        Validate service name follows naming convention
        Check for duplicate registration (same host:port:service)
        Persist registration with optimistic concurrency version
        Replicate registration to quorum of local DC nodes
        Trigger async cross-DC replication
        Notify watchers matching the service name and tags
        Return service ID and version for subsequent updates

Behavior DeregisterService
    Input: serviceId: string, reason: string
    Output: success: boolean, deregisteredAt: datetime
    Action:
        Validate service exists and requester has authorization
        Mark registration as deregistered with tombstone
        Remove from active DNS record set
        Notify all watchers of deregistration event
        Propagate deregistration to peer datacenters
        Schedule tombstone cleanup after retention period
        Emit deregistration metric with reason

Behavior ResolveService
    Input: serviceName: string, tags: list, datacenter: string, healthyOnly: boolean
    Output: endpoints: list, stale: boolean, queryTime: float
    Action:
        Look up service by name in local registry
        Filter by tags if specified
        Filter by datacenter if cross-DC query
        If healthyOnly, exclude endpoints with failing health checks
        Sort by health status and weight
        Return endpoints with staleness indicator
        Track query latency metric

Behavior PerformHealthCheck
    Input: serviceId: string, checkDefinition: HealthCheckDefinition
    Output: passing: boolean, responseTime: float, message: string
    Action:
        Execute check based on type (HTTP, gRPC, TCP, TTL, Docker)
        Measure response time against timeout threshold
        Update consecutive pass/fail counters
        If status transitions, update service health status
        If transition to failing and exceeds threshold, trigger deregistration
        Notify watchers of health status change
        Emit health check result metric

Behavior WatchChanges
    Input: serviceName: string, tagFilter: list, datacenterFilter: list
    Output: stream of ChangeEvents
    Action:
        Register watch subscription with filters
        Send current state snapshot as initial event
        Deliver subsequent changes in near-real-time
        Batch multiple changes within 100ms notification window
        Send periodic heartbeats to maintain subscription
        If watcher disconnects, buffer events for reconnection
        Clean up subscription on explicit cancel or heartbeat timeout

Behavior ReplicateCrossDC
    Input: operation: string, serviceId: string, payload: bytes, vectorClock: dict
    Output: acknowledged: boolean, conflict: boolean
    Action:
        Determine target datacenters for replication
        Apply vector clock comparison for conflict detection
        If no conflict, apply operation to remote DC
        If conflict, apply last-write-wins resolution and flag
        Await acknowledgment from remote DC
        If replication lag exceeds threshold, emit warning
        Track replication metrics per datacenter pair

# Level 4: Conditions
Condition: ServiceTTLExpired
    When service registration TTL expires without renewal heartbeat
    Then mark service as critical; after deregister-after-critical timeout, deregister the service; notify watchers of health transition; stop including in DNS resolution results

Condition: HealthCheckFailing
    When health check fails consecutiveFailureThreshold times
    Then transition service health to critical; remove from healthy DNS results; notify watchers; if deregisterAfter threshold reached, remove registration entirely

Condition: CrossDCPartition
    When replication to a peer datacenter fails for more than 60 seconds
    Then mark remote DC as partitioned; stop including remote endpoints in local queries; queue replication entries for catchup; emit partition alert; switch to local-only mode for affected services

Condition: WatchNotificationBacklog
    When pending watch notifications exceed 10000 entries per watcher
    Then drop oldest notifications; send snapshot-reset event to watcher; emit backpressure metric; consider increasing batch size or reducing watch scope

Condition: DNSQueryOverload
    When DNS query rate exceeds 10000 queries per second per resolver
    Then enable DNS response caching with extended TTL; rate limit per-client queries; redirect to alternative resolvers; emit DNS overload metric

# Level 5: Events
Event: OnServiceRegistered
    On new service instance registered in the catalog
    Action: Update local registry store, replicate to quorum, update DNS records, notify matching watchers, emit registration metric, begin health checking

Event: OnHealthStatusChanged
    On service health status transitions between passing, warning, and critical
    Action: Update service health in registry, modify DNS records if health-filtered, notify watchers with change event, emit health transition metric, trigger auto-remediation if configured

Event: OnCrossDCSyncComplete
    On replication catchup completes between datacenters
    Action: Verify consistency of synchronized records, resolve any detected conflicts, update global catalog, emit sync-complete metric with lag statistics, clear partition alert if active

Event: OnWatchSubscriptionExpired
    On watch subscription expires due to missed heartbeats
    Action: Remove subscription from active watchers, release buffered events, emit subscription-expiry metric, attempt to notify watcher endpoint if configured

Event: OnConflictDetected
    On conflicting writes detected during cross-DC replication
    Action: Apply conflict resolution strategy, flag entry for manual review, emit conflict metric, notify administrators if conflict rate exceeds threshold, log both versions for audit

# Level 6: Concurrency
Parallel:
    Health checking across all registered services
    Watch notification delivery to all active subscribers
    DNS query resolution on incoming requests
    Cross-DC replication streams to peer datacenters
    Registration and deregistration processing

# Level 7: Optimization
Optimize: DNS resolution latency
    Priority: Pre-compute DNS records for all healthy services; cache responses with appropriate TTL; use memory-mapped data structures for DNS record lookup; batch DNS record updates

Optimize: Watch notification throughput
    Priority: Batch notifications within coalescing window; use persistent connections for event streaming; compress notification payloads; implement backpressure-aware delivery

Optimize: Health check resource usage
    Priority: Adaptive health check intervals based on service stability; parallelize checks across services; use passive health checking from real traffic; aggregate checks for services on same host

# Level 8: Learning
Learn: Optimal health check interval per service
    Goal: Detect failures quickly while minimizing health check overhead
    Adapt: healthCheckIntervalSeconds per service
    Based: Historical failure detection time, health check pass rate, and service criticality tier

Learn: Service dependency topology
    Goal: Automatically map service dependencies for impact analysis
    Adapt: dependencyGraph for the service catalog
    Based: Service resolution query patterns, call graph data from tracing, and failure propagation patterns

Learn: DNS TTL optimization
    Goal: Balance DNS caching efficiency with responsiveness to service changes
    Adapt: dnsTTL per service
    Based: Service change frequency, client re-resolution behavior, and tolerance for stale endpoints

# Level 9: Security
Security:
    Encrypt: All registry API communication using TLS with service identity certificates
    Encrypt: DNS responses using DNSSEC with signed zone records
    Encrypt: Cross-DC replication traffic using IPSec tunnels
    Protect: Service registration via ACLs (register, deregister, read)
    Protect: Watch subscriptions against unauthorized access via token validation
    Protect: Against DNS cache poisoning via DNSSEC and DNS-over-HTTPS
    Protect: Admin operations (config change, force deregister) via RBAC with MFA

# Level 10: Native
Native: Go
{
package registry

import (
    "context"
    "sync"
    "time"
)

type ServiceRegistry struct {
    mu         sync.RWMutex
    services   map[string]*ServiceRegistration
    checks     map[string]*HealthCheckDefinition
    watchers   map[string][]*WatchSubscription
    dnsCache   *DNSCache
    replicator *CrossDCReplicator
    eventLog   *EventLog
}

func (r *ServiceRegistry) Register(ctx context.Context, svc *ServiceRegistration) (string, error) {
    r.mu.Lock()
    defer r.mu.Unlock()
    
    if svc.ServiceId == "" {
        svc.ServiceId = generateUUID()
    }
    svc.RegisteredAt = time.Now()
    svc.HealthStatus = "passing"
    svc.Version = 1
    
    r.services[svc.ServiceId] = svc
    
    // Replicate to quorum
    if err := r.replicator.ReplicateLocal(ctx, "register", svc); err != nil {
        delete(r.services, svc.ServiceId)
        return "", err
    }
    
    // Update DNS cache
    r.dnsCache.Update(svc.ServiceName, svc)
    
    // Notify watchers
    r.notifyWatchers(Event{
        Type:      "register",
        ServiceID: svc.ServiceId,
        Service:   svc,
    })
    
    // Log event
    r.eventLog.Append(Event{
        Type:      "register",
        ServiceID: svc.ServiceId,
        Timestamp: time.Now(),
    })
    
    return svc.ServiceId, nil
}

func (r *ServiceRegistry) Resolve(ctx context.Context, name string, healthyOnly bool) []*ServiceRegistration {
    r.mu.RLock()
    defer r.mu.RUnlock()
    
    var results []*ServiceRegistration
    for _, svc := range r.services {
        if svc.ServiceName != name {
            continue
        }
        if healthyOnly && svc.HealthStatus != "passing" {
            continue
        }
        results = append(results, svc)
    }
    return results
}

func (r *ServiceRegistry) Watch(ctx context.Context, name string, ch chan<- Event) error {
    sub := &WatchSubscription{
        WatchId:    generateUUID(),
        ServiceName: name,
        Active:     true,
        Channel:    ch,
    }
    
    r.mu.Lock()
    r.watchers[name] = append(r.watchers[name], sub)
    r.mu.Unlock()
    
    // Send current state snapshot
    r.mu.RLock()
    for _, svc := range r.services {
        if svc.ServiceName == name {
            ch <- Event{Type: "snapshot", Service: svc}
        }
    }
    r.mu.RUnlock()
    
    <-ctx.Done()
    
    r.mu.Lock()
    subs := r.watchers[name]
    for i, s := range subs {
        if s.WatchId == sub.WatchId {
            r.watchers[name] = append(subs[:i], subs[i+1:]...)
            break
        }
    }
    r.mu.Unlock()
    
    return ctx.Err()
}

func (r *ServiceRegistry) notifyWatchers(event Event) {
    name := event.Service.ServiceName
    if subs, ok := r.watchers[name]; ok {
        for _, sub := range subs {
            if sub.Active {
                select {
                case sub.Channel <- event:
                default:
                    // Backpressure: skip if channel full
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

description: AICL Example: Container Orchestrator Implements a container orchestration platform with scheduling, auto-scaling, self-healing, rolling updates, resource quotas, and pod-level lifecycle management.
instruction: Create an AICL specification for a container orchestrator. Include all 10 language levels: architecture (goals, constraints, risks with recovery, layers), entities, behaviors, conditions, events, concurrency, optimization, learning, security, and native code.
completion:
# AICL Example: Container Orchestrator
# Implements a container orchestration platform with scheduling, auto-scaling, self-healing,
# rolling updates, resource quotas, and pod-level lifecycle management.

# Level 1: Architecture
Goal: Provide a production-grade container orchestration platform that automates deployment, scaling, and management of containerized applications with intelligent scheduling, self-healing capabilities, zero-downtime rolling updates, and strict resource quota enforcement across multi-tenant clusters.

Constraint: Scheduler must place pods within 5 seconds of creation under normal load
Constraint: Rolling update must maintain at least 75% of desired replicas available at all times
Constraint: Resource quotas must be enforced at namespace level before pod admission
Constraint: Self-healing must detect and replace failed containers within 30 seconds
Constraint: Horizontal scaling decisions must consider both resource utilization and custom metrics

Risk: Resource starvation causing pod eviction and cascading failures
Recovery: Implement guaranteed QoS classes with resource reservations; enforce limits via cgroups; overcommit ratio capped at 2x for memory; OOM killer targets best-effort pods first; critical workloads have dedicated node pools

Risk: Rolling update stuck due to new pod version failing health checks
Recovery: Auto-rollback if progress deadline exceeded (600s default); maintain old ReplicaSet at scaled-down size for instant rollback; canary analysis with progressive traffic shift; manual rollback API

Risk: Scheduler hot-spot causing imbalanced resource utilization across nodes
Recovery: Implement bin-packing with spread constraints; anti-affinity rules prevent co-locating replicas; descheduler rebalances periodically; node auto-provisioning adds capacity when utilization exceeds 80%

Risk: StatefulSet volume detachment failure during node failure
Recovery: Force detach with verification after 60-second grace period; attach volume to replacement node; validate data integrity before serving traffic; implement volume replication for critical workloads

Risk: Resource quota violation through orphaned resources accumulating
Recovery: Periodic garbage collection of completed jobs and orphaned pods; resource quota accounting includes terminating pods; admission controller validates quota before creation; alert on quota approaching limits

Risk: Control plane failure preventing cluster management operations
Recovery: Multi-master HA with etcd quorum; leader election for scheduler and controller manager; cached state serves read-only queries during partial outage; etcd snapshots for disaster recovery

Layer: ControlPlane
    SubLayer: APIServer
    SubLayer: Scheduler
    SubLayer: ControllerManager
    SubLayer: EtcdCluster
Layer: NodeAgent
    SubLayer: Kubelet
    SubLayer: ContainerRuntime
    SubLayer: VolumeManager
    SubLayer: NetworkPlugin
Layer: WorkloadManagement

Optimize: Rolling update zero-downtime

Optimize: Cluster resource utilization

# Level 8: Learning
Learn: Optimal resource requests per workload
    Goal: Right-size resource requests to minimize waste while ensuring performance
    Adapt: recommendedCpuRequest and recommendedMemoryRequest per deployment
    Based: Actual resource consumption patterns over 7-day windows, P99 usage peaks, and OOM event history

    Adapt: targetUtilization and stabilizationWindowSeconds per HPA
    Based: Historical scaling event patterns, utilization oscillation frequency, and application warm-up time

    Based: Pending pod queue depth, node utilization trends, and cluster scaling history

# Level 9: Security
Security:

    Encrypt: etcd data at rest using AES-256 encryption

    Protect: Pod security via admission controllers (PSA, PSS)

{
package scheduler

import (
    "context"
    "sort"
    "sync"
)

type Scheduler struct {
    cache       *SchedulerCache
    framework   *SchedulingFramework
    binder      Binder
    queue       *SchedulingQueue
    metrics     *SchedulerMetrics
}

type ScheduleResult struct {
    NodeName    string
    Score       float64
    Evaluations int
    Duration    float64
}

func (s *Scheduler) ScheduleOne(ctx context.Context, pod *Pod) (*ScheduleResult, error) {
    start := time.Now()
    
    // Phase 1: Filter - find feasible nodes
    nodes, err := s.framework.RunFilterPlugins(ctx, pod, s.cache.GetNodes())
    if err != nil {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("no feasible nodes: %w", err)
    }
    
    if len(nodes) == 0 {
        s.metrics.RecordSchedulingFailure(pod, "no feasible nodes")
        return nil, ErrUnschedulable
    }
    
    // Phase 2: Score - rank feasible nodes
    scores, err := s.framework.RunScorePlugins(ctx, pod, nodes)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("scoring failed: %w", err)
    }
    
    // Phase 3: Select - pick highest scoring node
    selectedNode := s.selectHighestScore(scores)
    
    // Phase 4: Reserve - atomically reserve resources
    if err := s.cache.Reserve(pod, selectedNode); err != nil {
        s.metrics.RecordSchedulingFailure(pod, "reservation conflict")
        return nil, ErrReservationConflict
    }
    
    // Phase 5: Bind - persist scheduling decision
    if err := s.binder.Bind(ctx, pod, selectedNode); err != nil {
        s.cache.Unreserve(pod, selectedNode)
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("bind failed: %w", err)
    }
    
    result := &ScheduleResult{
        NodeName:    selectedNode,
        Score:       scores[selectedNode],
        Evaluations: len(nodes),
        Duration:    time.Since(start).Seconds(),
    }
    
    s.metrics.RecordSchedulingSuccess(pod, result)
    return result, nil
}

func (s *Scheduler) selectHighestScore(scores map[string]float64) string {
    type nodeScore struct {
        name  string
        score float64
    }
    var sorted []nodeScore
    for name, score := range scores {
        sorted = append(sorted, nodeScore{name, score})
    }
    sort.Slice(sorted, func(i, j int) bool {
        return sorted[i].score > sorted[j].score
    })
    return sorted[0].name
}

type SchedulerCache struct {
    mu       sync.RWMutex
    nodes    map[string]*NodeInfo
    pods     map[string]*PodInfo
}

type NodeInfo struct {
    Node              *Node
    RequestedCPU      float64
    RequestedMemory   int64
    AllocatableCPU    float64
    AllocatableMemory int64
    PodCount          int
    Images            map[string]bool
}

func (c *SchedulerCache) Reserve(pod *Pod, nodeName string) error {
    c.mu.Lock()
    defer c.mu.Unlock()
    
    nodeInfo, ok := c.nodes[nodeName]
    if !ok {
        return fmt.Errorf("node %s not found", nodeName)
    }
    
    cpuReq := pod.ResourceRequests["cpu"]
    memReq := pod.ResourceRequests["memory"]
    
    if nodeInfo.RequestedCPU+cpuReq > nodeInfo.AllocatableCPU ||
       nodeInfo.RequestedMemory+memReq > nodeInfo.AllocatableMemory {
        return fmt.Errorf("insufficient resources on %s", nodeName)
    }
    
    nodeInfo.RequestedCPU += cpuReq
    nodeInfo.RequestedMemory += memReq
    nodeInfo.PodCount++
    
    return nil
}

# AICL Example: Serverless Platform
# Implements a serverless/function-as-a-service platform with function runtime management,
# cold start optimization, event triggers, auto-scaling, billing, and execution isolation.

# Level 1: Architecture
Goal: Provide an elastic serverless compute platform that executes user-defined functions in response to events with sub-second cold start times, automatic scaling from zero to thousands of concurrent invocations, per-invocation billing, and secure multi-tenant isolation.

Constraint: Cold start latency must not exceed 500ms for interpreted runtimes and 2s for compiled runtimes
Constraint: Function execution timeout must be strictly enforced at configured limit (max 15 minutes)
Constraint: Concurrent invocations per function must scale from 0 to 1000 within 60 seconds
Constraint: Billing must be metered per invocation with 1ms granularity
Constraint: Function isolation must prevent cross-tenant data access and resource interference

Risk: Cold start latency spikes causing SLA violations during traffic bursts
Recovery: Maintain warm execution pool with pre-initialized containers; predictive pre-warming based on traffic patterns; reserved concurrency for latency-sensitive functions; snapshot-based restore for sub-100ms cold starts

Risk: Noisy neighbor causing performance degradation for co-located functions
Recovery: Strict resource isolation via Firecracker microVMs; per-function CPU and memory limits enforced by cgroups; network bandwidth shaping; dedicated worker pools for premium functions

Risk: Event source failure causing missed function invocations
Recovery: At-least-once delivery with idempotent execution; dead-letter queue for failed invocations; event source retry with exponential backoff; checkpoint-based offset tracking for stream sources

Risk: Runaway function execution consuming excessive resources
Recovery: Hard execution timeout enforced at runtime level; memory limit with OOM kill; CPU throttling via cgroups; per-function concurrent invocation cap; automatic suspension after repeated failures

Risk: Billing metering inaccuracy from distributed counter drift
Recovery: Atomic timestamped execution records; dual-path metering (real-time estimate + reconciled billing); periodic reconciliation with audit trail; per-invocation billing records persisted before response

Risk: Security breach via function escape to host system
Recovery: Defense in depth: microVM isolation, seccomp, AppArmor, read-only filesystem, non-root execution, network policies, and regular CVE patching; immediate quarantine on detection

Layer: FunctionRuntime
    SubLayer: ContainerPool
    SubLayer: ColdStartOptimizer
    SubLayer: ExecutionEngine
    SubLayer: ResourceEnforcer
Layer: EventIngestion
    SubLayer: TriggerManager
    SubLayer: EventQueue
    SubLayer: DLQProcessor
Layer: ScalingController
    SubLayer: ConcurrencyManager
    SubLayer: WorkerProvisioner
    SubLayer: ScalePredictor
Layer: BillingMetering
    SubLayer: ExecutionRecorder
    SubLayer: UsageAggregator
    SubLayer: InvoiceGenerator

Validation: Function deployment package must not exceed 250MB uncompressed
Constraint: Each function invocation must have a unique invocation ID for tracing
Validation: Reserved concurrency must not exceed account-level concurrency limit
Validation: Event trigger configurations must be validated before activation
Validation: Execution timeout must be enforced even if function code ignores signals
Validation: Billing records must be immutable once written

# Level 2: Entities
Entity Function
    functionId: string
    functionName: string
    runtime: string
    handler: string
    codeSize: integer
    memorySize: integer
    timeout: integer
    reservedConcurrency: integer
